Before designing a re-check for a moved check, ask whether there is even a second read to disagree with the first. | The active-campaign marker is opened once (O_NOFOLLOW, pre/post metadata equality), digest computed over the bytes read, and only the digest carried forward; relocating its cross-check earlier in the lifecycle was safe because nothing re-samples it. |
| A file-identity equality (dev+inode+mode+nlink) is NOT a content guarantee -- it typically excludes size, and an in-place rewrite preserving dev+inode+size defeats it. Anything needing content integrity carries a DIGEST; never re-derive content via the descriptor. State it at the descriptor type, because the next reader reads "stableIdentityEqual: true" as "same bytes". | StableFileIdentityV2 excludes size; harmless only because the digest carries content forward, exploitable the moment a future check re-reads via the descriptor. |
| A mention/reference count measures NAMING STYLE, not usage: designs (and code) name a path/symbol once and refer to it by role afterward, so a count of the literal is a floor near 1 regardless of real usage. Control on a path known to be used many times -- if it also returns 1, the instrument measures naming, not use; re-search by role. | A "single read" proof from a path-mention count of 1 was killed when authority.sock (certainly used repeatedly) also counted 1; re-search by role found the real usage sites. |
| When a new mechanism's BENEFIT scales with cross-instance references (dedup, sharing, symlinks, incremental deltas), its FIRST instance cannot exhibit the cross-instance FAILURE mode -- a first capture has nothing to dedup against, so the reference-resolution bug is structurally absent until the second. The acceptance gate must be the SECOND instance, never the first; a first-of-its-kind success is evidence about the first and silently not about the second. | PageDb shipped, gen 134 published with 43% dedup and restore-proven; the second capture died on cross-generation slab references the resolver could not see. The very property measured and celebrated (43% fewer objects) is the one that produced the failure. |
| A resolver's search set is a CORRECTNESS boundary, not a lookup optimization: it must search wherever a referenced object can LIVE, not where the current operation happens to write. A fix that adds "also search the prior generation" is a per-operation patch racing an unbounded reference distance; resolve by identity across all retained locations instead. | Dedup slice referenced a slab in an earlier generation's staging; narrow fix (search prior gen) re-breaks when a slice dedups against a base 2-3 generations back, which ages make MORE likely, not less. |
| The acceptance criterion for a VERIFIER is one falsifying vector PER COMPARISON, and its absence is a coverage defect of the same severity as the bug it would catch. A suite proving the verifier RUNS (happy path exercised) is not proving it GUARDS; the two claims differ and "green" reads as the second while meaning the first. Prove by deletion: each comparison removed must redden EXACTLY its own vector (and no other). | Nine of eleven comparisons in verify_bootstrap_exactness -- including the campaign-identity and connection-challenge checks -- were deletable with all 226 tests green: reached, happy-path-tested, never fed bad data expecting refusal. |
| Instrument bias toward finding gaps produces false-NEGATIVES-for-the-defence, not just false-positives-for-the-bug: a gap-hunting probe can hide a working guard. A no-op must never be able to print a passing result -- make the probe exit non-zero on a pattern miss so "no experiment" cannot masquerade as "no observer". | A leading-|| regex assumption hid campaignId, the ONE comparison that had an observer; an unescaped bun -e failed to parse and the harness printed test result: ok for fields the mutation never touched. |
| A string replace against FORMATTER-MANAGED source is not idempotent: cargo fmt (or any formatter) can reform the anchor between apply and restore, so print("restored") is a claim about what you tried, not what happened. Verify every restore by READING THE FILE BACK; grep for leftover markers before commit. A green suite after a mutation-restore is meaningless until the restore is confirmed -- the "failure" you see may be your own mutation still compiled in, which reads as a test-isolation bug. | An engram mutation restore reported success and changed nothing (fmt moved the anchor); a full suite then ran with the live mutation in, chased as parallel-test interference. Ended by instrumenting the assertion to print what it saw -- helper returning None with both dirs present -- pointing at the helper, not the fixture. |
| Engram enrollment has the silent-absence hole structurally: a malformed backup descriptor fails the fleet loudly, an ABSENT one produces no signal anywhere, so "is X backed up" is answerable only by a human happening to ask. Two modules (broca 1.2GB WAL, the vault store) found by asking, not by reporting. The fix is not "enroll X" (the instance) but "answer what is NOT enrolled" -- reconcile data-root contents against descriptors so absence is a reported state. | CKCRED had told Ufuk the APNs key exposure was bounded on the assumption the vault store was backed up; it never was -- a bound stated on a false premise, surfaced only because CKCRED asked. |
| Before deleting a FALLBACK (rollback binary, branch, snapshot, backup, feature flag), prove the thing it falls back TO is superseded -- not merely that you have identified the right file. Identity proof and safety proof are separate, and identity evidence looks equally complete whether or not the safety question was asked, which is what makes the omission dangerous rather than incomplete. A correctly identified rollback for a version STILL SERVING is exactly the one that must not be deleted. | THALAMUS's reclaim evidence proved the artifact WAS what they said; the fourth axis (running production carries the descent work the rollback lacks, running-inode==disk-inode) proved it was SAFE TO DESTROY. The look-alike pre-0567565 was correctly identified AND still-valid for a different live deploy -- deleting it would have passed every identity check. |
| A NUMBER THAT CHANGES ITS MEANING UNDER A STABLE NAME, read as a trend across the boundary where the definition moved. A series is a series only if every point is the SAME measurement; a stable field name is NOT evidence of a stable definition -- the definition moves silently exactly when a mechanism ships. Guard: when a mechanism change lands, any metric spanning it is a NEW series until proven continuous, and the burden is on showing the definition held. | Three in one day from engram: staged_bytes (whole-tree -> dedup-miss at digest-before-seal), entry_count (catalog entries read as chunks in a saturation alarm), "reusable objects" (per-object inventory_count 179k vs per-4KiB-page DedupMap rows 477k, spanning the PageDb enrolment boundary). The 460k step was enrolment, not runaway growth; the real rate was +174/gen, flat. |
| When a count is a PROXY for the real concern, disqualifying the count does not disqualify the concern -- restate the criterion on the quantity you actually care about, measured directly. | The livelock concern was cycle-time-exceeding-capture-interval; object count was the proxy. Proxy disqualified (unit change), criterion restated as generation wall-clock vs interval across 3-4 generations, measured directly. |
| A per-operation optimisation racing an unbounded state loses by default -- so a SECOND instance of the same fix is diligence, a THIRD is repeating a known-losing play. When the same fix is needed N times, ask whether the invariant is wrong one level down rather than patching N routes. | engram narrowed /state, then gc-preview and registry-projection failed the same wide-hydration way within hours. The defect is snapshot() (deep-clone of the object map) on the read path; the fork per route is fact-vs-set: bounded fact -> narrow SQL, genuinely needs every object -> streaming cursor. Never clone the map; do NOT build a general lazy layer (a third abstraction racing the same state). |
| Instrument the criterion BEFORE evaluating it; never compute something adjacent and call it the metric. And instrument a DISTINCT signal -- reusing an existing name invites the meaning-drift class. | Cycle-time (level-two) is unmeasurable: no published_at, and the nine "engram: published" hits are all the PageDb error string, so grepping "published" would return an error count dressed as cycle time. Fix: distinct capture-start/publish-complete lines, not a reuse of "published". |
| A paginated API over a fully-materialised backing is the most dangerous form of unbounded-state race: the interface ADVERTISES boundedness the implementation does not have, so it reads as already-fixed to anyone who checks the signature. Pagination bolted above a full materialisation bounds the OUTPUT without bounding the WORK. | engram's gc_preview asks for 256 rows and clones 477,611 to serve them; the cursor was real, the backing was a snapshot() deep-clone. Fix: cursor-bounded SQL LIMIT page_size, making the pagination honest. |
| When one operation's fix is needed N times, resolve at the invariant not the instances -- and verify the fork is real by checking each instance splits cleanly. Here: kill snapshot() on the read path (the deep clone is the defect); each route then picks narrow-SQL (bounded fact) or cursor-bounded-SQL (needs the set, a page at a time). No general lazy layer -- a third abstraction racing the same state is the same losing move renamed, and the tell is that it is a third move after two losses. | Two failing wide routes split one-per-branch: registry-projection clones 477k rows of a table it never reads (bounded fact, different collection); gc-preview touches 256 of 477k (needs the set, paged). |
| The standing question for reviewing a WIRE TYPE is not "is this diff correct" but "what does the OLDER side do with this" -- asked in BOTH directions (consumer older than producer, and producer older than consumer). A closed serde enum, a required new field, a narrowed type all read as locally correct and fail only at the version boundary neither repo can see from inside. It is a two-repo property, not a code-review property; reading the diff in its own repo never surfaces it. | QTA wrote, reviewed, and PR'd a closed PoolFunding/PoolBasis enum that read fine every time; one unknown variant from a newer insula would fail serde on the WHOLE entry in an older ALF/CKTUI/ck, dropping a healthy account's quota signal. Caught only by reading it as a consumer, not a reviewer. Fix: #[serde(other)] with a variant whose semantics match the fallback (Unknown funding = don't-spend; Unstated basis = treat-as-ceiling, honest about not knowing derivation). |
| A mutation result is evidence ONLY IF THE UNMUTATED BASELINE PASSES FIRST. "Both mutants caught" while the baseline is red is two meaningless readings dressed as a clean two-arm proof -- "the test failed" was true before you changed anything, so every mutant reads as caught. A two-arm mutation proof is actually THREE arms: mutant-A-reddens, mutant-B-reddens, and baseline-greens; the third silently validates the other two. Check the baseline separately; never read FAILED as confirmation. | PLEX's fix for a misrouted-transport fail-open had a red baseline (accept leg stripped a REST-only http block from action[0] when the fixture carried several -- single-element assumption again, this time inside the fix). Both mutants "caught" until the baseline was checked alone. |
| "Unroutable" fails safe (a confusing error, nothing happens); "misrouted" is the fail-open (accepted, stored as reviewed, dispatched to the wrong transport). A validator whose contract is "a stored X has been checked" accepting an X it cannot route is the contract violating itself -- and the fail direction is the difference between a filed nit and a security finding. | plexus router sent everything-not-rest_api to MCP while ingest validated only IS-rest_api, so a local_script manifest would issue an https MCP request to its transport.url. Fixed as a denylist of what cannot be served, so a new enum variant fails at ingest, not at dispatch. |
| A value whose job is to be unforgeable cannot have a second source of truth: a persisted/cached copy of a security fact is a drift surface, and a stale cache of a security fact is a forgery the system trusts. Memoizing a digest is sound ONLY if the memo key is a COMPLETE cover of the digested input -- the question is never "does the key change" but "can the INPUT change while the key does not". | engram's GC digest over (sweep_epoch, cutoff, generations, heads) + every admitted row: memoizing per-tuple is safe only if no write path mutates admitted-row membership/order without bumping a tuple component. Proof = a write-path enumeration with a defined negative (every membership writer moves a key component), not "the tuple looks stable". |
| When a memoization needs a stability proof, the incremental/streaming alternative needs NONE: chaining a digest through the page walk digests what it actually saw rather than trusting a key to stand for it. On a non-hot path (a GC sweep), pay the walk once. Memo if the cover-key proof closes (cheaper, reused); chain if it does not (safe unconditionally). | The dropped-page digest could memoize per-tuple OR chain across keyset pages; chaining is the unconditional-safe fallback because it recomputes over the rows walked. |
| A walk with a LIVE (unpinned) cutoff over a mutating set cannot be internally consistent: it observes a set that changes mid-walk and returns one number over it -- a torn read wearing a total's clothes, off by whatever mutated during the walk, in an unknown direction, with nothing in the number saying so. Memo-safety (the key changes so no stale reuse) does NOT redeem answer-consistency; they are different properties. Fix: pin the cutoff at walk start (snapshot even without a lease) or stamp the reader's contract "approximate, live cutoff". | engram's preview/lease-free path used cutoff=state.upload_seq_hi (moves every finalize); inventory_count over it is off by concurrent finalizes. The leased path pins cutoff at acquisition and is consistent; the preview path has no anchor to chain from, which is why it is categorically different, not merely softer. |
| A page-chain digest must commit to (a) its predecessor's digest AND (b) the rows this page saw in order AND (c) the page BOUNDARY (last id), so a dropped/split/merged page breaks the chain at that link and every link after. Chaining beats memo only if each link genuinely depends on the prior (linear, ordered) -- else a mid-walk dropped page leaves a valid-looking chain on both sides. A chain proves integrity only relative to an anchored head; a GC walk's anchor is the lease's pinned cutoff + sweep_epoch. | The memo enumeration found confirm_r2_delete removes an admitted row touching zero tuple components -- so removal must break the record and everything after it, which only a genuinely-dependent chain provides. |
| "Read the call site, not the comment" is right but INCOMPLETE: reading ONE call site and generalising is the same error one level up. An expensive computation that looks redundant against the consumer you found may be load-bearing for a consumer you did not grep. Enumerate ALL consumers before calling a computation redundant -- server-side AND client-side. | engram's O(inventory) per-page digest looked like an echo token: one server consumer (recompute-and-compare at plan submit), needed once, sent ~700 times. The "send it on the terminal page only" fix was killed by a SECOND consumer one grep away -- a client-side per-page assertion (main.rs:5883) that the whole-inventory digest is identical every page, which is the mid-walk-mutation detector for the already-walked PREFIX and the ONLY thing that catches confirm_r2_delete removing a row from a page already passed. The cost is irreducible given the property; the fix moved to the other axis (a resumable multi-tick walk), not a cheaper digest. |
| A page-chain that commits to predecessor+rows is blind to WHERE pages were cut unless it also commits to the boundary -- BUT if the pagination order is provably total and stable (keyset ORDER BY a unique column), the boundary is implicit in row order and committing to it separately is a redundant commitment, itself a small drift surface. Prove the order is total; add the boundary only if it is not. | Keyset pagination by unique object_id makes same-rows-different-pagination-same-digest impossible by construction, so the boundary commitment was not needed. |
| A forward running-chain is tamper-evident about the WALK, not about the STATE: once a row is folded in, the chain commits to "I saw row R at page N", which stays true even after R is deleted -- so a forward chain does NOT detect a removal in the already-walked prefix. Detecting prefix mutation requires re-reading the set (a whole-inventory recompute), which is inherently O(inventory) and not substitutable by any forward chain. If the property is required and its cost is a hard ceiling, move the fix to the OTHER axis: make the operation resumable across invocations (durable cursor + running digest + a PINNED anchor), not the digest cheaper. | engram's GC prefix-tamper-evidence: forward page-chain proves pages-walked-un-dropped, whole-recompute proves set-unchanged; you need the second and it must rescan. Resolution: checkpoint the walk against the lease's pinned cutoff+sweep_epoch so it resumes under the 32.5s CPU ceiling -- the pinned anchor (absent on the live-cutoff preview path) is what licenses multi-tick resumption. |
| A cover-key funnel maintained by an EXISTING correctness need (every writer must call it or something else breaks) is a STRONGER cover-key candidate and therefore a more convincing FALSE one: the completeness of the enumeration hides that a DERIVED field has inputs outside the funnel. Enumerate the inputs of the derived value, not just the writers of the row. | engram's mark_object funnel had 19 call sites, zero row-writers bypassing it -- airtight for row mutation. But gc_protected is derived from six collections; two (restore_pins, journal_intents) flip it via writers that touch no object row and call mark_object never. The perfect row-writer funnel hid the non-row inputs. |
| CORRECTION to the resumability row below (the whole premise was unmeasured and false): the digest was NEVER the cost. An adjudicator/reviewer who reasons about COST from a MECHANISM DESCRIPTION is doing what a worker reasoning from a smell does -- the profile is the only authority on what is slow, and a self-consistent mechanism story is the most dangerous input because it passes every check except the one that matters. MEASURE before ruling on cost; do not ratify a suspected cost through multiple design rounds. | engram GC: three rounds of resumable-walk design were adjudicated on "the whole-inventory digest is irreducibly expensive". Measured: BLAKE3 over 15.5 MiB / 477k rows = 8.7ms against a 32,500ms ceiling (0.03%). The real cost was O(N x 6 correlated EXISTS subqueries) SQL that rode in on the memory-fix commit, replacing an in-memory build-protection-set-once-then-O(1). |
| Two SEQUENTIAL failure limits are not evidence of a natural stack of limits -- the second may be one you just built. A clean-looking handoff between failure modes (memory-limit -> CPU-limit) deserves the same suspicion as a too-monotone A/B: "removed one ceiling and met the next underneath" vs "removed one ceiling and introduced a different one in the same commit" look identical until profiled. | engram read memory->CPU as a clean handoff; it was a regression introduced by the same fix that cleared the memory limit. |
| A per-tick/per-page invariant recompute does not become affordable just because the surrounding work is made resumable: resumability moves the O(page) work across ticks but leaves the O(whole) assertion per-tick. Measure whether the PROPERTY'S OWN cost fits one tick before designing resumption -- if not, the property must move (per-tick -> per-sweep, asserted once where a recompute already happens), not the schedule. And check which consumer is the real backstop: if a submit-time server recompute already catches the mutation, a per-page client recompute is defense-in-depth and can drop to per-sweep. | engram GC: ~477k-row whole-inventory rescan vs 32.5s CPU ceiling per tick is the gating measurement; the 5095 server recompute-and-compare vs the 5883 per-page client assertion is the which-is-the-backstop question that decides if the per-page cost is reducible at all. |

Prevention: state the premise IN the guard ("blocks because walks are scarce") so when the premise dies the guard visibly orphans; a guard whose reason lives in a commit message outlives its reason invisibly. | engram's deploy banner, true and useless within six hours of being written. Caught while mechanizing the walk-phase measurement note -- instruments audit their neighbours when they run together. |
| "MY CHECKING WAS LOAD": manual reassurance polls against a rate-limited endpoint count against the same limit as the watcher they reassure -- the observer-effect created by diligence, with a symptom (slow_down) that reads as a server-side condition to anyone who did not just write the second client. WHILE A WATCHER RUNS, READ ITS LOG; the correct number of clients against a rate-limited endpoint is one. | engram polled manually beside their 5s poller; both counted, server answered slow_down. |
| CLASSIFY PROTOCOL RESPONSES BY WHAT THEY DEMAND, NOT HOW ALIKE THEY LOOK: a STATE REPORT (pending -- demands patience) and an INSTRUCTION (slow_down -- demands behavior change) collapsed into one handler arm gives the instruction the state's response, which is no response -- escalating politeness into a refusal while looking patient. Sibling of the watcher-that-cannot-recognize-success: one misses the good terminal, this one causes the bad one. | engram's poller: one arm, three meanings ('pending'|'authorization_pending'|'slow_down'); fixed with backoff on slow_down. |
| KNOWING THE RULE DOES NOT INOCULATE AGAINST THE DEFECT: four faults on ONE hastily-written watcher (imagined counterpart, unrecognizable success, instruction-as-state, no heartbeat), written HOURS AFTER its author fixed the identical silence-hole in production code. The defect lives in the DEFAULT SHAPE of a quick watcher -- silence-when-fine -- so every new instrument gets run against the checklist explicitly; the author's fresh experience of the class is not a defense. "I keep writing detectors whose failure mode is silence, in a session whose entire subject is failures that were silent." | engram's device-flow poller, third iteration: heartbeat added (silence now means broken), slow_down in its own arm, success captured verbatim. The watcher watching for the credential that fixes capture finally holds the property the capture latch enforces. |
| AN EVENT THAT REPEATS A PAYLOAD IS NOT A SECOND OBSERVATION UNLESS IT CAN OCCUR WITHOUT THE FIRST (broca's test, adopted fleet-wide): a message_delta cannot arrive without a message_start, so it was never a candidate record -- model the pair as record+correction (field-wise last-wins into one accumulator), which closes the double-count class for every incrementally-reporting provider. The settling measurement for any minting reader: facts-per-run ratio (1.000 = correct; 2.0 = per-event minting). | Anthropic reports usage in BOTH message_start and message_delta with identical cache figures. Ufuk's doubled dashboard: engine ruled out by ratio (1997/1997), desktop app ruled out at source (renders counts, not percentages); the remaining reader of the raw stream is the dashboard's own ingestion. |
| SQLITE OPEN-MODE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE COMPANION FILES, NOT THE MODULE'S STATE: stopped-with-wal reads fine mode=ro; a companion-less file needs immutable=1 regardless of what the module is doing -- and whether a clean close REMOVES companions is a property of the SQLITE BUILD (daemon's 3.46.0 deletes them; Apple's 3.51.0 keeps them), so any module-state rule misleads on a host where a different binary closed last. `ls store.db-wal` is the whole rule. The completeness half outranks the open-mode half: A COMPANION-LESS MAIN FILE CONTAINS EXACTLY WHAT HAD BEEN CHECKPOINTED -- everything, nothing, or an arbitrary PREFIX -- and the prefix case opens, answers, and passes integrity_check while being short by an amount the file cannot report. Completeness comes from the audit chain, never from the file opening. | CKCRED's migration rehearsal reproduced the error-14 finding and corrected the rule (supersedes any "stopped module => immutable=1" phrasing; row 324 covers the live-database half). |
| SIX GREEN ACCEPTANCE LEGS LEAVE A NAMED RESIDUE: proving an insert cannot fail on schema (table present, exact columns) is NOT proving the writer's installed path, which is unreachable until a consumer meets the real trigger (a genuine 401). Mechanism-proven-path-unproven must be FILED as the gap, and the deferred acceptance SCHEDULED (check the table non-empty after the next incident), not remembered -- the logger built to catch silent failures can itself fail silently on its first real event. | CKCRED's auth_events: report_auth_failure has no live client; the first real 401 is the actual acceptance test, expected observable = one row. |

The eliminations were still worth having (each produced a reusable per-subsystem instrument); the ordering was the waste. | Cache-dashboard double-count: the surface was MC's own app (already fixed). Gateway, engine, and desktop each proved clean by subtraction before anyone named the actual surface. |

The stopping rule is not "split once" but SPLIT UNTIL EACH ARM'S FAILURE NAMES A DIFFERENT REMEDY (local data fault / keystore / cloud fact = three remedies, three arms). | engram's SlabWarmFailed: correctly named at the stage level, collapsed one level down; plus a fourth case silent entirely (wire present but will not open) reading as absence. |
| AFTER REMOVING THE HUMAN FROM EVERY PATH, GREP FOR THE PATH THAT STILL NEEDS ONE: the rebuild path built its cloud target with the account-JWT-only constructor while every other path minted worker tokens -- the ONE remaining success that depended on a human login, hidden because the account JWT usually existed as a side effect of other ceremonies. A tap "fixing" it buys minutes (necessary, not sufficient -- captures refused INSIDE the JWT's valid window, measured); the durable fix is the minting constructor with fallback to prior behavior so a mint refusal cannot become a capture refusal. The audit: enumerate call sites of the credential-bearing constructors and ask which can run unattended. | engram 3be71d5: cloud_target_for_publish vs cloud_worker_target. The device-auth work (July) de-humanned every path except this one. |
| A MARKER THAT CANNOT DISCRIMINATE IS ALSO A CLAIM ABOUT THE BUILD THAT CAN BE FALSE: the deploy ladder's marker table verifies PLACEMENT, but a marker reading 0 in your own build catches a BUILD defect -- containment proves what execution coverage cannot. First instinct was instrument error (strings(1) merging/fragmenting are real effects) -- the raw-binary grep adjudicated: tool right, code wrong. | engram 0a8d31d: dead line removed, all four cause markers then discriminated 1/0. Third marker-table catch in one day, first on a defect rather than a placement error. |
| LEVEL-VS-EDGE ADMISSION: A THRESHOLD PREDICATE USED AS AN ADMISSION GATE ADMITS THE BAND, NOT THE CROSSING. A level ("fill above X") is true on every pass while the condition holds, so gating a first-application on it works on sessions that VISIT the band (admits once-ish, reads as batching) and degenerates to per-pass admission on sessions that LIVE in the band -- which is exactly the workload whose own reclaim is too small to exit the band, so the case that most needs batching defeats it. Why it survived review: the gate DID catch the original defect and its regression test asserted that case; a band pass IS a legitimate execute pass by every local signal, and distinguishing "crossed this pass" from "still inside" requires history the predicate does not carry. Fix shape: sidestep (ride-only semantics on independently-qualifying passes) rather than encoding edge detection. | MC supersession lane 2026-08-11: 15 self-caused prefix rebuilds / 592K cache-creation tokens in 60 passes ON THE BUILD THAT SHIPPED THE FIX; live-verified to 0 after. Diagnosis joint MC+THALAMUS. |
| PARENT (THALAMUS, third member with aged-pin equality and observation-armed gates): these predicates are EVALUATED AT THE WRONG MOMENT rather than computed wrong -- each is correct at exactly one instant, which is why all three survive unit tests: A TEST NATURALLY CHECKS THE INSTANT THE AUTHOR HAD IN MIND. Defence: WHEN A PREDICATE IS CORRECT AT ONE INSTANT, THE TEST MUST RUN AT A DIFFERENT ONE (assert per-pass across N defer passes individually; age the live side past the seam; post-descent windows). | Generalisation THALAMUS, incident MC supersession lane 2026-08-11. |
| A DURABLE PROGRESS ROW AND A LIVE PROGRESS ROW LOOK IDENTICAL WHEN READ ONCE: "IN FLIGHT 158 pages" was where the last GC slice PARKED (a durable cursor), not an active walk -- a parked cursor wears an active walk's clothes. Dual of the resetting-counter rule: a moving counter proves something runs but not what; a STATIC row proves nothing about whether anything runs. Both resolve identically -- a second reading at a known interval -- and when two surfaces go static together with a held socket, stop inferring and SAMPLE THE PROCESS: 1,616 of 1,755 samples in CloudTarget::get_object is not ambiguous. | engram's rebuild fetch phase: walk row static (parked), staging static (fetch not done), TLS held, CPU 1% -- indistinguishable from a wedge by inspection; the stack settled it in one sample run. |
| CPU ACCRUAL IS A FREE PROGRESS METER FOR ANY SEQUENTIAL WORK LOOP: when a fetch/decrypt/hash phase has no counter, cputime-per-completed-item turns the process's own accounting into a rate proxy (1.9% busy at ~decrypt+hash cost per slab -> ~78min projection), and TWO ESTIMATES FROM UNRELATED QUANTITIES AGREEING (cpu-accrual ~78 vs round-trip arithmetic ~90) is the strongest confirmation a counterless surface allows. When built: per-N lines carry a running ABSENT count (the data-fork early warning must not wait for completion), and a persisted cursor states its live-vs-parked discriminator at the schema comment. | engram's rebuild fetch phase: three acceptance surfaces all static and all correct mid-fetch -- identical to a wedge; resolved by process sample + accrual proxy. FALSIFIED AS THIS INCIDENT'S CAUSE IS NOT DISPROVEN AS A HAZARD -- different verdicts about the same code (the unfixed priority inversion stays on the daylight list). |
| THE CONVEYOR VARIANT (MC addendum, 3rd family member same day): A WATERMARK DESIGNED FOR BAND VISITS (advance once per crossing) INVERTS UNDER BAND RESIDENCY into a per-pass conveyor -- each pass advances the watermark and mints the previous pass's arcs as newly eligible. The level-gate variant RE-ADMITS; the watermark variant RE-MANUFACTURES ELIGIBILITY, and the second compounds (9.6% of all input at cache-write rate over 520 passes). Fix confirmed sidestep-over-edge-encoding twice: ride-only + watermark frozen while waiting, advancing only when the batch applies. Coda (corrected by MC after THALAMUS collapsed the decomposition): the incident was TWO mechanisms, not three -- the conveyor (this entry, unchanged) and a missing durable m0-end breakpoint on the CC leg (56,654 floor byte-constant across 31 recurrences while m0 ranged 8 sizes: the discard was the whole conversation, not a migrating anchor). The two refuted limbs died on shape facts: the backward-moving marker was a SYMPTOM (27 moves, zero with an intact prefix -- every one a fold), and the migrating-anchor hypothesis projected one leg's split-block shape onto another's single-block wire. | A NUMBER MOVING IN A SUSPICIOUS DIRECTION IS NOT THE DEFECT -- THE DISCRIMINATOR IS WHETHER THE THING THE NUMBER DESCRIBES ACTUALLY CHANGED (THALAMUS, twice in one night): reclaim counts moved because the array changed under the members (the lane never acted); a marker index moved backward with ZERO surviving cached bytes (nothing to regress). Both times the discriminator was one measurement away -- check what the number DESCRIBES before reporting its direction as the finding. | The direction-reading sibling of the two-true-denominators rule. |
| WITH A SINGLE OBSERVATION THERE IS NO WAY TO DISTINGUISH "UNCHANGED, CORRECT" FROM "MOVED, WRONG BY THE DELTA EVER SINCE" (ASTRO): a first fresh fetch resolves the ambiguity FORWARD and cannot resolve it backward, so the permanent cost of a stale snapshot is the AUDIT, not the history -- rates that never moved were priced correctly all along, but nothing can recover WHICH ones those are. Interim posture: STATE the conditional authority ("authoritative only for rows unchanged since <date>") rather than papering it. Companion catch: the "lane" being replaced was a hand-staged file behind an mtime gate -- a decoy pipeline that looked like ingestion; check whether the thing being migrated away from ever ran before pricing the migration. | astrocyte price_snapshot: 5,297 rows at one observed_at_ms, hand-staged 19 July, zero multi-era models. | A FIXTURE AUTHORED FROM THE SAME MISUNDERSTANDING AS THE PARSER CERTIFIES THE DEFECT WITH A NON-VACUOUS ASSERTION: the commons tier parser read keys models.dev never emitted (context_over/min_context), and its test asserted min_context == 200_000 AND PASSED -- because the hand-written fixture supplied the invented key. No mutation of the test could catch it; the fixture and parser encode ONE wrong belief, so they agree by construction. The escape: EXECUTE the parser against REAL upstream bytes (FUSI found 335/335 thresholds parsing to 0 on the live payload, silently, 183/183 providers "successful"). Cleanest specimen yet of the fixture-provenance rule: produced-output fixtures must be minted by the real producer. Fix direction matters too: missing threshold now REFUSES loudly (a tier whose floor defaults to 0 applies its over-threshold rate to everything -- silent repricing), and a second test pins that the legacy invented keys DO NOT satisfy the parse, so a compatibility tidy-up reddens by name. | commons ffdd06a (0.2.0). Found by FUSI on their first day, by measuring instead of reading. ASTRO's 251 stored rows stay poisoned until re-ingest; the fix stops the bleeding, never heals history. |
| AN APPEND-ONLY EFFECTIVE-DATED STORE CONVERTS BAD DATA FROM A TRANSIENT STATE INTO PERMANENT HISTORY: re-ingest adds a correct ERA, it does not clear the poisoned one -- every point-in-time query into the bad era returns the bad values forever, CORRECTLY (the ledger must say what it stored when). "Healed" is a property of ERAS, never of stores: consumers need an era floor (no reads before the first post-fix era), not an assumption that re-ingest made the store uniformly good. Companion credit rule: a control credited that does not exist (an unfinished feature praised as a deliberate gate) gets trusted by the next person exactly when it matters -- refuse the credit, record what actually defends. | ASTRO's price_snapshot: 251 min_context:0 rows are permanent 19-July-era history; the defense is the recorded poisoned-until-reingested prerequisite, added AFTER the report, not the unread tiers_json. Refinement: the era floor must be PER-FIELD, not global -- a later correction touching a different field would otherwise raise the floor for fields it never touched (why correction EXTENT, not just a marker, belongs in the correction record). |
| WHEN A DEPENDENCY BUMP ADDS A REFUSAL SURFACE, LAND IT AGAINST INPUT WHOSE ACCEPTANCE IS PROVEN BY REPETITION -- "cannot refuse" must mean disprovable-by-the-run (same bytes parsed 5,297 rows every tick for 23 days), not "has not refused so far": a merely-lucky input leaves a first failure with two candidate causes, which is the entanglement the split exists to remove. If no repetition-proven input exists, bump and cutover are entangled whether or not they are separate commits -- say so rather than split-and-claim-isolation. Bump-and-cutover as one change makes a genuine upstream malformation indistinguishable from a cutover bug on the first failure. ASTRO's split: 0.2.0 against the 23-day-static hand-staged file first (same bytes parsed 5,297 rows every tick -- refusal provably unreachable), THEN the automated-source cutover separately. One variable per change, applied to a version bump. | The loud-failure path and the untrusted-input path must not go live in the same instant. |
| THE STATE OF MIND THAT WRITES A FIX IS NOT THE STATE OF MIND THAT FINDS A DEFECT, and one hour between them changes nothing: a fix for "we assumed context_over was the threshold key" shipped while still assuming tier.type was "context" -- the SAME failure mode, one field over, in a commit written specifically to close that failure mode. The practical form: a fix to an assumed-field-meaning defect gets a deliberate sweep BEFORE shipping -- "which other fields does this function read whose meaning it does not verify?" -- which in the proof case would have found both residuals (the type gate and the missing row context) in one pass. Catching each other's fixes works only while both parties happen to be looking. | commons ffdd06a -> 528b680 (FUSI's pushback). Companion audit form, mechanically checkable with no domain knowledge: WHEN ONE VARIANT IN AN ERROR ENUM LACKS THE CONTEXT ITS SIBLINGS CARRY, THE OMISSION IS USUALLY ACCIDENT, NOT DESIGN. |
| IDENTITY CHECKS ANSWER "IS THIS THE BUILD I PINNED", NEVER "IS THE FIX IN THE BUILD I PINNED": LC_UUID, lockDigest, and both-arms pins make an artifact's identity unforgeable while saying nothing about its CONTENT -- a staged pair everyone called ready was SIX COMMITS SHORT of the fix it was said to deliver, and placing it would have passed the whole identity ladder while leaving the defect running, with every seat recording the deploy as the remedy. A deploy justified by a specific defect needs a CONTENT check naming that defect (ancestry: fix-sha is an ancestor of build-sha; or marker: defect-specific string 0-in-old/N-in-new with a both-builds control), run at approval time, not staging time. | PLEX caught 1a2368d predating gap-fix ee5e321 at the moment of deploy; rebuilt at HEAD c01be00. The ritual gap was ours fleet-wide: two exchanges spent making identity unforgeable, zero asking whether it contained the fix. MECHANICAL FORM (PLEX follow-up): binaries embedding their build commit (build.rs) self-report from the FILE via strings -- so step 0 runs at approval time on the staged artifact, unplaced and unrun: embedded=$(strings <staged> | grep -oE <sha-pattern>); git merge-base --is-ancestor <fix-sha> $embedded. READ THE EMBEDDED VALUE, NEVER THE FILENAME -- the name is a claim, the embedded commit is a measurement, and they diverge exactly when someone rebuilds under a reused name. Three-arm probe requirement (anchored-grep instance #4: ^sha$ returns 0 on packed Rust literals): staged/its-commit=1, deployed/its-commit=1 (probe works), deployed/OTHER-commit=0 (probe discriminates) -- without arm 3 a match-everything grep also passes. |
| PRE-REGISTRATION PROTECTS AGAINST SHAPING THE PREDICTION AFTER THE FACT, NOT AGAINST GETTING THE MECHANISM WRONG: a step registered before the window still carried two wrong assumptions -- it attributed the OLD binary's writes to the NEW one (baseline taken pre-bounce; the old build kept polling during 41s of placement -- measure from PROCESS START, the only boundary separating builds), and it expected the wrong property (a fix that SETTLES legitimately re-detects each conflicting item once before going quiet; "counts unchanged" fails correct behaviour -- the bound is distinct conflicting items, not zero). A pre-registered step's first REAL run is itself a test of the step. | PLEX step 8, corrected in 9863064 after reporting FAIL on a working fix. |
| A ROLLBACK ARTIFACT IS A BINARY AND THE CATALOG IT ACCEPTED, OR IT IS NOT A ROLLBACK ARTIFACT: a bare rollback binary restored under a newer catalog fails the whole boot (the old build refuses fields the new catalog carries at ingest). Pin the rollback bundle as binary+config, and prefer the bundle over any loose staged binary of the same build. | PLEX's rollback-20260811T122529 (binary + 17-file catalog) vs the bare ck-plexus.7702590 -- same binary, only one is restorable. |
| STEP 0 NEEDS THREE VERDICTS, NOT TWO: git merge-base --is-ancestor exits 0 (ancestor), 1 (not ancestor), 128 (unresolvable ref) -- and an embedded commit with a -dirty suffix is NOT A GIT REF, so a naive if/else collapses "fix genuinely absent" (rc=1) with "cannot evaluate" (rc=128) and reports a missing fix for an uncommitted tree, sending someone to REBUILD (which reproduces the same dirty marker). rc=0 PASS, rc=1 FAIL, anything else ERROR naming the unresolvable value -- a check whose input cannot be evaluated must say so, never pick a side. Dirty markers get STRIP-AND-FLAG: the ancestry question is still answerable from the recovered clean sha, but the answer must ride with "built from an unclean tree", which is itself deploy-refusal grounds. Modules WITHOUT a dirty marker have an unambiguous but WEAKER check (proves the fix is in the named commit, not that the built source matched it) -- the argument for the marker, not against. | PLEX measured all three exit codes before the norm propagates; the dirty build is the COMMON accident (build mid-edit, ends up staged), not the edge case. |
| THE SWEEP QUESTION ONLY FIRES IF SOMEONE ASKS IT -- THE STANDING INSTRUMENT IS WHAT MAKES ASKING CHEAP (FUSI's fragility note on their own form): the state that produces a REPORT is as committed to its framing as the state that produces a fix (they filed the tier report with the payload open and did not check tier.type either). What made both residuals findable was a probe that ALREADY EXISTED -- testing "does it accept a non-context tier" was a two-line edit to a standing binary, not a project. TREAT THE INSTRUMENT AS THE DELIVERABLE: a probe that parses real bytes and prints structure outlives every question it was built for, and the sweep is cheap exactly where one is standing. | Companion to fix-state/find-state: the question is fragile, the instrument is durable. FUSI keeps theirs. |
| OWNERSHIP AND LOCATION ARE SEPARABLE, AND CONFLATING THEM MANUFACTURES FALSE DESIGN CONFLICTS: "who authors the schema and controls its evolution" (fusiform) and "where is it published from" (commons) are different questions -- the coupling worth avoiding is LOCKSTEP RELEASES, which semver publication prevents and in-place editing by whoever-needs-a-field creates. Sequencing trap the split exposes: designing types in your own repo and migrating to the published slot later is a BREAKING change for every adopter; starting in the published slot costs nothing now. | FUSI reconciling BROCA's "separate type, not an extension" with the commons-from-day-one amendment: both right, the conflict was in the framing. |
| SPLIT DURABILITY BY TRIMMABILITY: an UNTRIMMABLE log (tamper-evident audit chain -- trimming is the exact thing the evidence is defined against) gets STATE TRANSITIONS only (`AND state <> ?2` makes a repeatable write a transition; repeats match zero rows); the TRIMMABLE table gets everything, bounded per-credential. The repeats are not lost -- they land where bounding is possible. Mutation pair worth copying: the plausible OVER-FIX (also skipping the trimmable row) passes the audit assertion while destroying the evidence of the loop it exists to diagnose -- the disambiguating arm is what catches the fix an author would actually ship. | CKCRED 4d9eadf: 8 identical reports = 8 chain entries, 7 changing nothing; found by taking "no-op-to-write conversions inherit an unbounded-growth obligation" as an INSTRUCTION to enumerate what else grows per-event -- the sweep-the-property rule executed same-day on the ledger note's own subject. |
| AN ACCEPTANCE CRITERION WRITTEN WITHOUT READING THE PATH IT PREDICTS DESCRIBES A SYSTEM THAT MAY NOT EXIST -- and its passing or failing then measures the author's model, not the code.
