| ONE-SHOT CURATIVE PLUS PROSPECTIVE ELIMINATION BEATS A STANDING RECOVERY ARM: when a fix has two halves (tombstones make future orphan heads nameable; a recovery arm heals the one existing victim), ask whether the prospective half makes the recovered-from state UNREACHABLE -- if yes, a standing recovery arm is permanent security-critical code for a state the same cut eliminates, and the curative half should be a one-shot audited operation instead (verify lineage from durable storage, adopt under a logged command, done). A standing arm is what you build when you CANNOT eliminate the state. The detector's honest blindness message ("no exact local staged row remains") is the model for code whose witness was deleted: report the blindness, refuse, never guess. | engram gen-144 recovery design; the two-arm read at source (ObservedStagedHead requires the deleted row; Equivocation refuses every tick). |
| A RECORD SCOPED FOR HUMANS MAY BE AN INPUT THE CODE NEEDS: the tombstone was nearly built as a diagnostic aid (so the anomaly line would read better) when it is actually the MISSING OPERAND of the recovery discriminator -- the cosmetic version would have shipped a nicer error over the same permanent refusal. When designing a record, enumerate its CONSUMERS: if any consumer is a comparison rather than a reader, the record is load-bearing and its schema must serve the comparison. Companion: A COMMENT CAN STATE AN INTENT THE IMPLEMENTATION'S INPUTS CANNOT SATISFY -- "distinguish our own stranded publication from a foreign head" requires knowing what was EVER published, while the consulted set holds only what is STILL staged; the design was right, the data source too narrow, and the prose promised a distinction the code could not draw. Fix shape: the three-way test (staged -> adopt; known-retired -> ours, adopt; neither -> refuse loudly) implements the comment's original intent. | engram discriminator at cloud.rs:2672-2688; the tombstone upgraded from prospective hygiene to the actual repair by reading the comparison it feeds. |
| DISPATCH-TIME PRE-EMPTIONS THE RANKER OWES (the ranking rule closing its loop): two store-decidable facts read BY THE BRIEF-AUTHOR before the worker could guess -- (a) NAME-COLLISION PRE-EMPTION: an existing table (retired_roots, 0 rows, plausible name, unrelated stage-2 machinery) is exactly the prior art a diligent worker would find and wrongly extend; naming it and saying why not converts a wrong turn into a sentence -- the worn-name class handled at dispatch. (b) THE HONESTY GRADIENT IN BRIEFS: "a thing to check, not a fact I assert; I have not read its writers" -- a guess wearing authority in a brief becomes the worker's premise, and premises from authority do not get re-derived; label open questions as open. (c) NAME OPERATIONAL CONSTRAINTS (live store, daemon holds the lease -> migration-at-startup vs repair-on-demand) and require the tradeoff ARGUED rather than the tidy option picked -- elegance that cannot execute is a review round. | engram tombstone dispatch, second iteration; both facts one command each, both would have cost the worker a wrong turn. |
| A COMMENT THAT POINTS AT ANOTHER FILE FOR ITS RATIONALE HAS OUTSOURCED THE THING IT EXISTS TO SUPPLY (BROCA's self-correction): "same rule as the restart gate" is a cross-reference the reader standing in THIS file cannot resolve -- it rots, moves, and transfers nothing; state the reason itself. Companions from the same close: PROVE EVERY FAILURE ARM BY CAUSING IT before trusting a checker's green (baseline-lowered/empty-tree/unreadable-input each forced to fire -- a checker whose failure arms never fired is the instrument-that-never-disagreed); and the DOUBLE-DUTY ACCEPTANCE TURN proven in production: a deploy check reading real state (SUBC_COMPAT) returned the exact sibling HEAD pinned an hour earlier from the other direction -- the check audits the state and the state audits the deploy. | broca v0.3.34 close; the finalize-leak witness ships with a frozen baseline of 4 and prints its count on success. |
| A BRIEF THAT CONSTRAINS THE INVARIANT AND LEAVES THE MECHANISM OPEN GETS BETTER ANSWERS THAN ONE THAT SPECIFIES BOTH -- provided the invariant is stated sharply enough that a wrong layer is visibly wrong (engram's capstone on the tombstone dispatch): the brief required same-fenced-transaction and left "where does the tombstone live" open; the worker chose the store layer, where a future delete path CANNOT forget the write -- the mandatory-over-conventional answer the brief-author had not specified. Division of labor: the invariant is the ranker's (they own the consequences), the mechanism is the worker's (they can out-derive the ranker on it), and the sharpness condition is what makes delegation safe rather than hopeful. | engram tombstone worker's layer choice; the walk's closing witness reads "the defect's own trigger continuously present for three hours, producing nothing" (56 deferrals frozen under a pinned backlog). |
| COUNT THE REFUSALS AFTER A PERMISSIVE-LOOKING CHANGE: a three-way classifier split that ADDS a recoverable arm is proven non-weakening by the refusal paths MULTIPLYING rather than disappearing (four surviving terminal sites beside the new arm) -- the anatomical read that distinguishes a split detector from a bypassed one, cheaper than any test. Companions from the same delivery: the derive-not-accept instruction found a THIRD delete site the brief-author did not know; the honest-gap clause returned a deliberate non-tombstone WITH its reason (a fixture simulating historical deletion would be invalidated by a current-schema tombstone); and the argue-don't-pick instruction produced a lease argument reasoned FROM the constraint ("migration does not silently inject account-specific evidence") rather than around it. A brief's meta-instructions (derive, report gaps, argue) are what convert a worker from an implementer into a second deriver. | engram tombstone delivery (wi_20d01176): three-way classifier, tombstones at all three derived delete sites, backfill as audited ManagementSurface op with trigger-proven atomicity. |
| SCORE THE DELIVERY, NOT THE REPORT (engram's settlement note, worth the rubric's margin): a worker whose worktree was reclaimed mid-suite produced an EXEMPLARY memory-reconstructed report (observed vs inferred distinguished exactly where it mattered) over a delivery that needed real closing work (three tests, one gate, five guards closed by the reviewer, plus a shared-fixture defect that cost a separate task) -- scored 88, not higher, because scoring the report's quality would teach the router that reconstruction excellence substitutes for finished work. The paired lesson from the 94: the top score was REACHABLE because the brief's meta-instructions (derive the delete-site set, report gaps with reasons, argue the mechanism) let the worker out-derive its author on the load-bearing parts -- initial-delivery scoring and derivation-granting briefs are two halves of the same routing signal. | engram triple settlement (94/93/88), ledger clean; all three scores on initial delivery per the rubric. |
| AN HONEST STATUS FIELD PAYS OUT ON ITS FIRST REAL AMBIGUITY: the tick=DEFERRED (run kind N holds the scheduler; counters are pre-run) annotation -- added hours earlier because a health cache claimed a per-tick refresh that never happened -- was the single line that distinguished "healthy module running an expensive capture" from "wedged scheduler" when every observable froze at once. Without it the payload read as healthy-idle-with-frozen-counters, and a plausible-but-wrong starvation mechanism was already being constructed from the novelty of a recently-changed gate. Companions: FOUR STALLED READINGS WERE FOUR PROJECTIONS OF ONE RUNNING JOB (correlated freezes can mean one healthy cause, the evidence-legs lesson in reverse); and MECHANISM-FROM-NOVELTY is a named trap -- "this is the first time condition X has held since I changed Y" makes Y the suspect by adjacency, when the observable may have a simpler single cause; check the cheap process/status read before theorizing the new code. | engram post-adoption freeze; resolved by the author's own six-hour-old honesty annotation, two self-corrections issued. |
| TWO FIELDS, TWO QUESTIONS -- A FIELD ANSWERS ONLY THE QUESTION IT WAS BUILT FOR: staleness:fresh described the scheduler's CADENCE while capturesRunning described the PRESENCE OF A RUN; reading the first as answering the second manufactured an instrument disagreement that never existed in the state (an "idle" verdict from a freshness field while a run held the guard). The field's QUESTION belongs in its name or its docs -- and the disambiguating instrument was a THIRD surface with different failure modes (staging directory mtimes), which killed two live theories in one listing (no accumulating dirs = no capture loop; an actively-written dir = no phantom deferral). Companion pin: a row created at START is not evidence of completion (maxseq flat during a running capture is correct, not stalled) -- know which lifecycle edge each counter stamps. | engram gen-148 capture; the reads disagreed, the state never did. |
| "THE OUTAGE IS OVER" AND "EVERYTHING IS CORRECT" ARE DIFFERENT CLAIMS, MAKE ONLY THE ONE YOU CAN PROVE: closure was claimed on the pre-registered condition (fresh capture published to a head descended from the adopted commit; pubhead 143->148, unpub 0) and NOT on the classifier recognizing the head 40 minutes earlier -- while two same-window anomalies (journal refusals, a zero-page walk slice) were named as open rather than absorbed into the win. Post-outage triage rule: A CLOSED DEFECT FAMILY REAPPEARING IN THE RECOVERY WINDOW IS FIRST CHECKED AS THE OUTAGE'S OWN DEBRIS (dead publish attempts bound journal seqs that the succeeding publish collided with) -- the discriminator is whether fresh instances appear on the NEXT clean cycle, not whether any appear during recovery. The equivocation taught this exact shape hours earlier: the mechanism's residue misread as the mechanism's recurrence. | engram outage closed: 14 hours, five narrowed legs, a tombstone, an adoption, and a 3,964-object publish in one cycle. |
| A LOG LINE NAMES A FAMILY, AND THE READER SUPPLIES THE DEFECT: refusal lines from the intent-binding family were read as the family's FAILURE returning when they were its REMEDY operating (same seq refused with two object ids, then step-forward -- the persisted binding correctly detected as different and correctly stepped past; 49 lifetime firings, zero lost publishes). Third form of the mechanism-vs-residue lesson in one night: a mechanism's residue, its recurrence, and its OPERATION all wear the same log vocabulary -- read the SEQUENCE, not the line. Companions: one orphaning event leaves MULTIPLE kinds of orphaned state at different layers (a deleted generation orphaned both the head -- fixed by tombstone+adoption -- and its intent bindings -- self-healed by stepping), so a repair at one layer does not retire the family; and A SELF-HEAL COUNTER IS A SUCCESS TALLY THAT READS LIKE AN ERROR TALLY -- the label chooses the category, so name it for what firing MEANS (healed), not what it looks like (refused). | engram post-outage triage; the alarm self-corrected by reading three consecutive lines instead of one. |
| A DELTA ACROSS A COUNTER RESET IS MEANINGLESS WITH BOTH OPERANDS CORRECT: slice_pages = total_after - total_before reported 0 for a slice that fetched 24 pages, because an epoch reset put the operands in DIFFERENT EPOCHS (before=676 old epoch, after=24 new) and saturating subtraction floored the difference. The delta family's second mechanism in one night: the watcher's +56 came from an UNSET operand; this 0 from VALID operands spanning a boundary. Fix shape: deltas are meaningful only within an epoch -- stamp the epoch on both operands and refuse cross-boundary subtraction, or accumulate slice-locally instead of differencing cumulative reads. The instrument was added THE SAME NIGHT to read resumed walks honestly, and the one unconsidered boundary (epoch reset) was immediately exercised by the night's biggest event (head change invalidating the inventory) -- new instruments meet their edge cases fast. | engram zero-page slice; both post-outage anomalies closed as recovery artifacts, account healthy end to end. |
| A DIAGNOSTIC THAT CANNOT READ IS WORSE THAN NO DIAGNOSTIC -- it manufactures the appearance of the problem it was built to clarify: a quota diagnostic built its target without a worker token (read-before-mint, the same class as the 24h GC outage and the outage-opening defect), fell back to a JWT expired BY DESIGN, and failed on every tick for weeks -- reporting its own failure in the vocabulary of the thing it was watching. It decoyed a credential-outage investigation for a full round and the mint hunt besides. Audit rule: paths whose OUTPUT is failure-vocabulary (diagnostics, probes, health reporters) get the read-before-mint sweep FIRST, because their failures are camouflaged as findings by construction. The reasoning belongs in the doc comment at the fix site so the next reader inherits the why. | engram 401 wart, closed as the first defect's sibling after two clean post-outage cycles; rides the next cut with the slice-delta fix. |
| CAPABILITY-BEFORE-CONSISTENCY GUARDS FIXES, NOT JUST DIAGNOSES: a plausible mechanism (delta across an epoch reset) was supplied by the adjudicator, endorsed with a fix shape, and NEARLY BANKED -- the source read killed it in thirty seconds (both operands come from one walk state in one invocation; the cross-epoch story is not what the code implements). A repair shipped for a plausible-but-wrong mechanism "fixes" code that was not broken that way, leaves the real defect standing, and banks a false mechanism in the ledger. CORRECTION HYGIENE: revert the ledger entry to the OBSERVATION WITHOUT THE EXPLANATION -- a real observation with an open mechanism invites the right next reader; a false mechanism misleads them. And when two numbers DISAGREE WITHIN ONE LOG LINE, the next step is mechanical: trace each field of the emission site to its source variable -- one of your assumptions about which value the logger prints is wrong. | engram zero-page slice, round 2; the adjudicator's theory died at the seat's source read, fix correctly held. |
| A DEFENSE WRITTEN IN A COMMENT PROTECTS ONLY THE READER ALREADY READING CAREFULLY: a field-scope comment ("a number whose scope is not in its name gets compared to whatever looks compatible") saved the THIRD reading of a confusing log line and not the first two -- those were made at speed from the log line alone, where the comment does not travel. Scope belongs in the FIELD NAME (slicePages vs pagesFetchedCumulative): the name travels with every emission, the comment stays home. Sequence note for the file: THREE MODELS TRIED, TWO RETIRED AT SOURCE, ONE STANDING ON THE CODE'S OWN WORDS (epoch-delta -> intra-line disagreement -> honest zero from a resumed cumulative), each retirement cheaper than the fix it prevented; the residual (one 62s zero-page fetch in the noisiest possible window) stays an OBSERVATION with a pattern trigger (a second instance outside such a window), not a mechanism. | engram zero-page slice, closed as non-defect on the third source read. |
| A THEORY FROM A TRUSTED PEER IS STILL A THEORY (engram's attribution correction, sharper than the adjudicator's version): the failure was not ACCEPTING the peer's epoch-boundary mechanism -- it was RECORDING IT AS SETTLED (with a fix direction) before reading the code. Trust changes who you listen to, not what counts as verification. Companion hygiene: when a mechanism dies, update the ledger to resolved-with-DISCARDED-MODELS-RECORDED so the next reader inherits the dead ends rather than rediscovering them -- the stranded-work lesson applied to explanations. | engram zero-page close-out; two wrong models retired in ten minutes, no code changed, both recorded. |
| A CHECK THAT ONLY FIRES WHEN YOU REMEMBER TO RUN IT IS THE SAME CLASS AS A COMMENT THAT ONLY HELPS THE READER ALREADY THERE (engram's second single-copy recurrence in one night): the origin/master..HEAD hygiene sweep caught production-running-on-unpushed-source TWICE, both times unprompted -- proving the detection works AND that detection-by-memory is not prevention. The mechanism is structural (push belongs to no phase of deploy tempo: build->verify->place->watch), so the fix is a HABIT WITH A TRIGGER: push-before-place as a ladder step. Placer-side twin: before placing any artifact, verify its source commits are pushed -- the placer can check as cheaply as the builder, and two independent habits beat one. | engram night close: 3 autonomous cycles, head 143->149, backlog 0; second push caught by the same sweep that caught the first. |
| "FIXED ON MASTER" AND "FIXED IN PRODUCTION" ARE DIFFERENT CLAIMS, AND THE GAP CAN CONTAIN A KNOWN DECOY: a close-out stated commits as pushed-and-CI-green in a way that invited reading them as deployed -- while a decoy log line that had already cost a full investigation round (the 401 quota-diagnostic) STAYS LIVE until the next placement, printing credential-vocabulary that means nothing. When a fix is committed but unplaced and its defect is a DECOY, pre-register the expectation ("this line is expected until placement") so the next reader inherits the explanation instead of the investigation -- tombstoning applied to a log line. The tense taxonomy generalizes: past-tense claims anchor (built at SHA), present-tense claims rot (running in prod), and deploy-state sentences must say which they are. | engram CI close; fourth autonomous cycle underway, fix rides the next real cut. |
| LC_UUID IDENTIFIES A (COMMIT, PATH, TOOLCHAIN) TRIPLE, NOT A COMMIT (CKCRED's measurement: the same commit built in the main tree and a worktree produced two different LC_UUIDs). SURVIVES: same-artifact identity across one placement (staged == placed == running under signing/copying -- the ladder's use). DIES: recovering "which commit is this running binary" from the UUID, or rebuilding candidates until one matches -- the incident-time use, where you hold the binary and nothing else. Fleet convention adopted from their pattern: `<name> <version> (<rev>)` answered BEFORE any config gate (an identity check must not depend on the thing being identified running correctly), CK_BUILD_REV injected by the release script at build time (not build.rs shelling to git, which reruns per-commit and rebuilds the graph), "unknown" when unstamped rather than a guess, and the release script REFUSES ON A DIRTY TREE (a stamp naming a commit whose contents were not what was built is worse than no stamp). Note subconscious's half-instance: ck-subc embeds BUILD_COMMIT but serves it only over the wire -- identity-if-running, the same critique one layer up. | claustrum deploy-verification correction; ck-claustrum e34ad77 staged, rides the next window. |
| A FROZEN COUNTER'S EVIDENTIARY VALUE COMPOUNDS WITH ELAPSED CYCLES: at repair time, the frozen equivocation count proved the classifier STOPPED MISFIRING; four autonomous cycles later the same 18 proves THE ADOPTION IS DURABLE -- a fix that recognised the head once but failed to persist recognition would have re-fired on cycle two. Repair vs resolution is distinguishable only with elapsed cycles; let the account run before declaring the stronger claim. Companion, closing a three-instance night: THE DEFENSE MUST BE WRITTEN WHERE THE CONFUSED READER WILL BE -- comment vs log line (scope in the field name), project memory vs log line (a pre-registered decoy explanation reaches future sessions, not a human tailing the log), check vs habit (push-before-place as a ladder step). One shape: a defense's value is its LOCATION relative to the reader, not its correctness -- and where possible, retiring the confusing artifact beats explaining it anywhere. | engram gen-150 close; cadence autonomous, counter frozen through four readback cycles. |
| A TEST SUITE CANNOT VERIFY A STAGED ARTIFACT: CARGO_BIN_EXE_* resolves per-profile and cargo rebuilds before running, so `cargo test --release` spawns a binary it JUST BUILT -- never the one staged. Proven constructively: the release binary was DESTROYED and all 8 e2e arms passed. "e2e green, ship it" feels like artifact verification and is not; a green suite says the SOURCE is good and nothing about the shipped bytes -- only post-placement acceptance legs see deployed bytes. Companion: STAGING INTO A DIRECTORY CARGO OWNS means any later cargo invocation silently replaces the artifact (a staged, signed binary was rebuilt-over within one command; the pre-publish sha stopped describing the file, and the backup captured the REBUILT binary so the restore was wrong too -- caught only by hash comparison). Stage into a rev-keyed directory outside target/ and verify by rebuilding afterward with the staged sha unchanged. Accepting a staged path from a peer now includes checking it is outside any cargo-owned tree. | claustrum morning-batch prep; two publishing-process defects found by the author verifying their own artifact before handoff. |
| A FAIL-LOUD REQUIREMENT IS ONLY CORRECT WHERE THE DEPENDENCY IS OBTAINABLE (BROCA's CI fix): a vault e2e's binary requirement was folded into the CI-wide gate -- but CI checks out only two of the three repos, so the gate demanded a binary it could never have; requiring what the environment cannot supply does not make the run stricter, it makes it UNIFORMLY RED, which carries the same information as uniformly green. Conditional gates ship with the three-arm proof: the exempt condition skips, opted-in-without-dependency fails NAMING THE SWITCH, dependency-present runs the real test. Companion instrument note: A VERSION SUBSTRING IS NOT A VERSION MARKER -- `strings | grep 0.3.35` read 11/10 because the OLD binary contains "0.3.35" ten times inside catalog price literals (0.3135 etc.); the count would have read "already deployed". Use the binary's own --version output, which is unconfounded. | broca v0.3.35 placement; fresh live-runs read at placement time per the staleness rule (the 20-minute-old refusal had cleared). |
| STRUCTURAL ACCEPTANCE IS NOT SEMANTIC AUTHORITY, AND A MINT FROM UNVERIFIED BLOBS IS LAUNDERING AT THE TRUST ROOT (cortexkit-e2e's ninth refusal, the one that protected trust rather than correctness): the accumulator proves framing/cardinality/ordering/aggregate arithmetic and NOTHING semantic -- fixtures with EMPTY signature and SPKI fields pass today because nothing checks them, and a mint consuming those blobs would have compiled, gone green, and placed unchecked authority at the point every downstream trust decision rests on. The parity parser REFUSES a frame claiming semantic authority (stronger than defaulting to false) -- the design's own statement that authority must come from verifiers, not framing. Sequencing shape for verifier families: ORDER BY CONSUMPTION NOT SIZE (the capstone's largest dependency first; its rejection surface teaches the family), each slice delivers the NEGATIVE VECTORS for its own arms (today's silently-passing fixtures become tomorrow's named rejections), and the capstone states consumption AS A TYPE CONSTRAINT (accepts only witness types the verifiers produce -- unverified input unrepresentable, not checked for). | bootstrap-v2 epoch mint blocked on a real scope gap; nine refusals, nine correct, master green throughout. |
| A DEFERRAL'S REASONING MAY NOT COVER WHAT THE BLOCKED ARMS ACTUALLY REQUIRE -- RE-MEASURE BEFORE INHERITING IT: three YAML manifest arms were about to inherit a months-old defer-all-YAML ruling whose reasoning was about SERIALIZATION (byte-equality with npm yaml stringify = an unverified differential with no oracle). But two of the three are ExactSourceYaml -- bytes-as-authored, verifiable by digest plus parse-only semantics, needing no serializer at all; and the third (CanonicalYaml) may not need a PORTED serializer either, because a frozen member set needs canonical bytes of SPECIFIC KNOWN MEMBERS, pinnable as producer-minted fixtures (run the real JS serializer once at fixture time, verify by digest at runtime -- the pin-at-the-producer rule; the oracle exists, invoke it, never port it). A blanket deferral inherited by name rather than by reasoning converts a 15/15-verifiable mint into a false 12/3 partition. Companion capstone rule: A MINT ACCEPTING VERIFIED WITNESSES PLUS EXPLICITLY-DEFERRED BLOBS is unverified input made representable in costume -- if arms are genuinely unverifiable, the honest state is capstone-blocked, never a partition mint. | bootstrap-v2 manifest-member scoping; the collision with the F2 YAML deferral dissolved by reading what each encoding label actually obligates. |
| NEVER PUBLISH A HASH FOR A PATH A BUILD TOOL OWNS (CKCRED's general form -- the directory does not have to be target/ to bite), and its release-pipeline completion: point the e2e suite at the EXACT STAGED FILE via an env override SET BY THE RELEASE SCRIPT, so artifact verification is structural rather than remembered. Four arms proven by construction: corrupt-staged-binary FAILS where the --release run PASSED (the suite now sees shipped bytes); restore passes; nonexistent-override-path REFUSES rather than falling back to the cargo-built binary (a typo'd override silently testing the wrong file reports exactly the green the caller wanted); script verify-step exits 101 BLOCKING -- because a verification step that warns gets read hours later, at deploy time, when the binary looks like any other. | claustrum 6daf3af staged for the morning window; finding closed rather than documented. |
| A DEFERRED-UNTIL-NEEDED DEPENDENCY DECISION IS A DECISION MADE UNDER SCHEDULE PRESSURE: a choice that "only has to land before the capstone" becomes urgent the day the capstone is ready, with the slice waiting on it. Open the gate the day the need is IDENTIFIED: draft the dependency case (candidates, maintenance, transitive footprint against the lockfile, the spec's rejection list restated as named negative vectors, the differential oracle) while other work builds, so the decision sits APPROVED when its consumer arrives. The bootstrap-v2 YAML sequence for the record: a deferral inherited BY NAME would have yielded a false 12/3 partition; re-reading the encoding labels' OBLIGATIONS yielded 14/1; the lockfile fact (zero YAML crates; all three arms need a PARSER regardless of serialization) reframed the question into a materially different decision than the deferred one. | bootstrap-v2 manifest-member: 12 JSON arms dispatched, YAML parser gets its own evidence-gated decision now. |
| A PARSER THAT SILENTLY RESOLVES ANCHORS OR MERGE KEYS MAKES THE REJECTION UNOBSERVABLE (cke2e's YAML-crate selection criterion): when a spec REQUIRES rejecting a construct, a library that helpfully RESOLVES it away passes every functional test while making the forbidden thing invisible -- resolution-as-convenience is the fail-open shape at the library-selection layer, and it disqualifies candidates no functional test would flag. Selection specs for dependency gates should name the constructs that must surface AS ERRORS, not merely parse correctly. Companion counting rule: ARITHMETIC ON REMEMBERED COUNTS CONFLATES POPULATIONS -- "12 = 15 transmitted minus 3 YAML" was wrong because the arms are 16 PROJECTIONS (13/3); the same projections-vs-members conflation produced two wrong numbers in one thread, both fixed by measuring the registrations file. And: an arm with an EXISTING verified capability is CONSUMED, not re-verified -- with the expectation of its absence (no frame) asserted, so the untransmitted projection is a checked property rather than a silent gap. | bootstrap-v2 13-arm slice dispatched; YAML parser case drafted-unapproved at its own gate. |
| CO-DEPLOYED ARTIFACTS GET CO-VERIFIED: driving a staged daemon with a cargo-built CLI proves NEITHER -- the wire between a deploying pair is exactly where a mismatched build shows, so both suites take both overrides, and the incident-tool half (the CLI an operator reaches for mid-repair) is the higher-stakes artifact because its failure is discovered while repairing something else. AND THE TECHNIQUE'S HONEST BOUNDARY: A TEST REACHING THROUGH A cfg(debug_assertions) SEAM IS STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE OF VERIFYING A RELEASE ARTIFACT -- release builds compile the seam out ON PURPOSE, so the arm verifies source, never shipped bytes; both halves are correct (the bypass must compile out, the test must not reach a live provider) and the honest resolution is a skip that PRINTS ITS REASON, with such arms enumerable in advance by grepping for the cfg. Companion: a test comparing a staged binary's version against the TEST'S OWN compiled BUILD_REV is the self-referential gate in harness clothing -- one side of any comparison must originate outside the thing under test. | claustrum pair 5d6cd83; corruption proof 11/12 arms fail; rides the morning window. |
| ACCEPTANCE HAS AN OWNER-SIDE LEG BY CONSTRUCTION: a placement ladder proves IDENTITY and LIVENESS (sha, inode, version, health) but reads are unfenced -- a fenced-out daemon serves reads perfectly while refusing every write, so only a FENCED WRITE moving durable state (mint+revoke advancing the audit tip) proves AUTHORITY, and only the module owner can burn one. Companions from the same close: SEAMS THAT ALTER A DECISION vs SEAMS THAT RELOCATE STATE (an injected env short-circuiting validation narrows artifact verification; one relocating XDG paths is production mechanism -- pin the DECISION-seam count in the release script so a new seam is a named choice, not silent narrowing); and A VERIFICATION GATE THAT CANNOT DISTINGUISH CONTENTION FROM DEFECT WILL EVENTUALLY BLOCK A GOOD DEPLOY ("did not publish within 15s" reads identically for crashed, mis-built, and busy at load 6-9; the gate now reports process-liveness + load + which reading they imply). Host contention has produced false readings on three instruments this week -- gates must name their own ambiguity. | claustrum pair 5d6cd83 accepted both sides, six legs including the owner-side fenced write. |
| A DIAGNOSTIC WHOSE ACCESS REQUIREMENTS CONTRADICT THE STATE IT DIAGNOSES HAS, IN PRACTICE, NEVER RUN (CKCRED's vault finding): verify-audit took the single-writer lease, so it required the daemon STOPPED -- and nobody takes the credential vault down for an integrity check, so the check justifying the entire HMAC chain went six weeks unrun. A tamper-evidence mechanism nobody can afford to invoke provides evidence of nothing. THE TEST: does the diagnostic run in the state it is meant to diagnose? (Not "is it correct" -- correctness was never in question.) Sibling of the empty-store operator-path rule: that catches capabilities unreachable from a fresh store; this catches diagnostics unaffordable in the live state; both invisible from inside the module, both found by REACHING FOR THE VERB. Companions: TWO MEANINGS SHARING ONE ALARM WORD (169/172 flagged rows were routine admin writes drowning the 3 real anomalies -- flag both loudly, name them differently); and guidance advising a remedy that does not exist (exit-3 advising --subc for a verb with no admin op) is its own small class. | claustrum verify-audit, now lease-free: 1435 entries verified intact against a LIVE daemon for the first time. Fleet canvass queued. |
| SELF-CANVASS RESULT (subc, applying the diagnostics-state test to my own house first): every ck verb (module, health, quota, daemon, rescan preview) runs over channel-0 against the LIVE daemon -- all diagnostics run in the diagnosed state by construction, so CKCRED's stopped-system class does not reach them. THE INVERSE GAP IS REAL THOUGH: every subc diagnostic REQUIRES the daemon running and reachable, so the one state ck cannot diagnose is the daemon's own failure -- a down or wedged daemon reduces ck to a connection error, and the operator falls back to manual archaeology (start-lock presence, connection-file staleness, log tail). Same family as identity-if-running: the tooling answers every question except the one asked during a daemon outage. A `ck daemon triage` verb that reads ONLY disk state (lock, connection file mtime + pid liveness, log tail) and never dials would close it -- parked as a candidate for the next subc cut alongside the --version convention. | fleet canvass fired (engram, broca, more to follow); subc's own answer recorded first. |
| THE DIAGNOSTIC-AVAILABILITY TAXONOMY (three modules, three mechanisms, one outcome): ACCESS-GATED -- the check requires a state nobody can afford (CKCRED's verify-audit took the single-writer lease = daemon stopped; never ran in six weeks). AVAILABILITY-INVERTED -- every check requires the component that might itself be broken (subc: all ck verbs dial the daemon, so a daemon outage is the one state the tooling cannot diagnose). CADENCE-GATED -- the path runs on a long timer and the deliberate invocation that would exercise it takes a guard that refuses during busy windows (engram's gc.run: 7-day sweep cadence, guard-gated manual fire). Unifying rule: A PATH THAT RUNS RARELY IS A PATH WHOSE DEFECTS ARE ALWAYS FRESH -- the walk-starvation bug lived its whole life in such a path. Canvass method note: engram answered by ENUMERATING all nine RunGuard::acquire sites rather than arguing from architecture -- the read costs minutes and converts "should be fine" into "absent from the list". | fleet diagnostics canvass, first three answers; engram's backup.verify proven runnable-in-state by enumeration. |
| FOR PATH-DEP CONSUMERS THE VERSION BUMP IS THE ONLY SIGNAL THAT REACHES THEM AT ALL (FUSI+BROCA, verified in the consumer's own lockfile: a path dep appears with NO source and NO checksum while a registry dep carries both -- Cargo.lock cannot pin a path dep, so nobody consumes the published version and semver protects nothing). The wire-crate version-bump CI check is therefore LOAD-BEARING, not hygienic -- and that reasoning belongs IN THE SCRIPT, because the next reader will see a version check and assume semver is doing the work. Companion: A PRECEDENT READ AS INFRASTRUCTURE IS INVISIBLE AS PRECEDENT ("I went looking for a house pattern in subc-protocol and did not recognise I was looking AT it") -- patterns must be NAMED as patterns somewhere findable, or each new module rediscovers or reinvents them. | fusiform-protocol minted on the module-owned-payload ruling; version discipline mechanized with three-way proof, golden-fixture half honestly declared unbuilt. |
| A SHARED HELPER ASSERTING ON ITS CALLERS' BEHALF, WHERE THE ANSWER IS ONLY KNOWABLE AT THE CALL SITE (CKCRED's second layer): open_for_admin was marked true for one caller's sake and a second caller silently inherited advice wrong for it -- one message serving two situations reads as correct from either side alone, and there is NO VANTAGE POINT INSIDE THE HELPER from which the conflict is visible. The two-emission-paths bias inverted: one path, two callers, the guard's TEXT diverging instead of its logic. Fix shape: the discriminating fact travels FROM the call site; the shared site never invents it. Test shape: assert BOTH ARMS TOGETHER so the lazy fix (collapse to one message) fails on the arm it degrades, then mutation-verify by collapsing -- a discrimination test, not a wording test. Canvass sharpened to its historical form: HAS THIS DIAGNOSTIC EVER RUN AGAINST A SYSTEM IN THE STATE IT DIAGNOSES -- past tense, recoverable from shell history, answerable by evidence rather than architecture argument. | claustrum remedy-text discrimination; pair 5a1f233 staged for the next window. |
| RIGHT QUERY, RIGHT ANSWER, WRONG EXPLANATION -- AND THE WRONG EXPLANATION PREFERRED BECAUSE IT SHRANK THE WORK (cke2e's tenth-refusal retraction): a grep for constructions correctly returned zero, and a type-theoretic story (phantom markers, idiomatic, plausible) explained the zero WITHOUT READING THE STRUCT -- which had a concrete stored field, making zero constructions a real gap. The tell: WHEN AN EXPLANATION OF A MEASUREMENT MAKES WORK DISAPPEAR, the explanation gets a source read before any narrowing ships. Companion ruling: WHEN TWO DERIVED ARTIFACTS DISAGREE (a scaffold vs a catalog), NEITHER IS THE AUTHORITY -- the design text is; if the design names the owner, the disagreeing artifact is simply wrong (evidence lean: the measured artifact thirteen arms build against outranks speculative code with zero constructions); if the design is SILENT, the silence is the finding and takes a normative amendment, not a pick. A slice built on either reading before the design speaks encodes a guess as authority -- laundering, one layer up. | bootstrap-v2 authority-projection retraction; fork parked on the design read. |
| FOUR INDEPENDENT ARTIFACTS AGREEING THROUGH DIFFERENT MECHANISMS is the anchored form of a design verdict (cke2e's arm-2 confirmation): a design clause naming the owner, catalog dispatch with zero overlap, frame-budget line items with separate caps, and cap prerequisites naming two distinct histories -- four legs with DIFFERENT FAILURE MODES, not four views of one writer. The decisive clause was the ELEVENTH of fifteen grep hits -- read-past-the-first-hit validated twice in one thread. Correction discipline: A FIX THAT MOVES AN ENUM ARM WHILE THE CONSUMER STILL DEMANDS IT FROM THE OLD FAMILY RELOCATES THE UNSATISFIABLE INSTRUCTION -- measure the consumption site before writing the slice (the thread began with a scaffold that outran its spec; the correction must not do the same). And a REMOVED arm gets a NEGATIVE VECTOR (the wrong-family construction unrepresentable or rejected by name) so a future author who finds the absence puzzling cannot reintroduce the defect. | bootstrap-v2 authority-projection fork resolved: scaffold wrong, catalog+design agree, fix approved pending the consumption measurement. |
| A PATTERN IS VISIBLE ONLY WHERE THE ALTERNATIVE IS ALSO VISIBLE (FUSI's sharpening, superseding the name-the-pattern rule): a shipped artifact carries no trace of the option it beat, so "subc-protocol lives in subconscious" reads as a fact about a repository while "wire types live with the producer RATHER THAN in commons, because producer ownership makes drift unauthorable" reads as a rule -- same files, and only the second is findable as precedent by someone who does not already know the answer. Naming must include what was chosen OVER. Companions from the same close: pick golden-fixture cases for THE FIELDS A CONSUMER READS WHEN SOMETHING IS WRONG (that is when nobody regenerates fixtures); and a wall-clock field in a fixture gets a PLACEHOLDER (so renames still diff) PLUS a separate bracketing assertion (value between two clock reads) -- a substituted field with no live assertion is a hole wearing a key. | fusiform outputs half closed at 83b07ff; both halves of the payload rule in at 38 commits. |
| THE FOURTH FORM: RUNS-BUT-DOES-NOT-DISCRIMINATE (BROCA, completing the diagnostic-availability taxonomy): a verb that executes cleanly in the live state while concurrency has dissolved its discriminating power -- one byte cut from a WAL tail (what a reader sees mid-append) turned "REGRESSION: 1 leaked" into "no new leaks", a verdict over records the walker never decoded, presenting as a CLEAN RUN rather than a refusal so nothing signals the loss. The proving move: TAKE A KNOWN POSITIVE AND DAMAGE IT THE WAY LIVE TRAFFIC WOULD -- testing an instrument against an idle system only ever shows the answer you want. Fix family: the walker reports whole-file consumption and the scan REFUSES (cannot-compare) on any file ending mid-frame -- the same honest refusal as the unreadable arm. Full taxonomy: access-gated / availability-inverted / cadence-gated / runs-but-does-not-discriminate. Happy inverse on record: broca's read path (pure in-memory decode, no write handle -- a correctness invariant, since a truncating reader would kill an active run) gave every diagnostic lease-freedom FOR FREE -- architecture sometimes answers the canvass, but only running the verbs makes it evidence. | broca canvass answer; wal-verify 19,021 files/1.74GB live in 10s, witness hardened against torn tails. |
| THE FIFTH FORM: RUNS AND STRUCTURALLY CANNOT SUCCEED (engram's R42 GC find, revising their own canvass answer): the sweep fired, proposed, was refused on an all-or-nothing plan containing one protected member, and -- with deterministic candidate ordering -- reproposes the same poison row forever; the single ledger row READ AS CADENCE because a refused run and a rare run leave identical evidence. What was filed as cadence-gated was defect-blocked -- only reading the predicate pair found it. THE CLASS: TWO PREDICATES ANSWERING ONE QUESTION FROM DIFFERENT LISTS (selection covered six protections, revalidation seven; the missing generation_registry clause invisible from either side alone -- each side complete against ITS OWN list). CKCRED's shared-helper defect inverted: two sites, one question, no vantage point seeing both. Fix: derive both predicates from ONE protection source (shared view / single registry_protected_ids call) -- hand-patching the missing clause into selection reopens the gap the day an eighth protection class lands on one side. Fail-direction credit: all-or-nothing rejection made this a LIVENESS bug, not data loss -- the conservative gateway performed its job while selection starved it. Taxonomy now five: access-gated / availability-inverted / cadence-gated / runs-but-does-not-discriminate / runs-and-cannot-succeed. | engram generic GC structurally unable to reclaim on retention-enabled accounts since shipping; fix pending the retention-eligible arm verification. |
| A JAM THAT CADENCE MADE INVISIBLE (the rare-path rule's concrete instance, one hour after banking): the GC predicate gap is THREE states wide (ActiveRetained, RetirementEligible, Quarantined) and Quarantined poisons the D phase too -- so Q AND D are jammed by one selection/revalidation disagreement, and the account's 92.6/128 GiB with retention configured is not slow-cadence accumulation but a machine that has NEVER reclaimed. A refused run, a rare run, and healthy quiet leave the SAME ABSENCE; only the predicate read discriminated. Scope-revision honesty: "fail-closed held" survived while its consequence inverted from "Q is slow" to "reclamation has never existed" -- both true, state both. Fix gates: the protection-state list derives from ONE shared constant (or the eighth-state day reopens it), and DIGEST PARITY between the two projections is an explicit gate -- two implementations of one protection set with divergent digests is the same defect reborn inside the fix. The witness that proves the PATH unjammed (not just Q): a D-phase deletion actually completing for the first time. | engram reclamation jam, full scope; fix dispatched with digest-parity gate. |
| A CHECK THAT ANSWERS A NARROWER QUESTION THAN ASKED SHOULD SAY SO (FUSI's improvement, adopted upstream): the wire-crate version check compares COMMITTED history only, so "clean" with uncommitted wire-crate edits sitting in the tree reads as tree-consistency while meaning commit-consistency -- it now prints the narrowing when crates/ is dirty (note to stderr, exit unchanged). Meta-instance while adopting it: MY FIRST PROOF WAS VACUOUS -- both arms printed usage (missing base-ref) and the grep -c 0/0 read as clean/clean; I committed on it, then re-proved with the argument supplied (0/1/0 across clean/dirty/restored). A proof whose command refuses is not a proof that passes -- check the instrument ran before reading its answer, ESPECIALLY when banking someone else's lesson about instruments. | check-wire-crate-versions.sh 11733471; the boundary-predicate class (era BEGINS-in vs SPANS window) also banked from FUSI's correct-guard defect. |
| THE PROBE CREATED THE PHENOMENON IT OBSERVED (FUSI's third and nastiest measurement failure of the day): testing whether ck-models would appear in ck's domain list via PATH="/tmp:$PATH" put fifty scratch ck-* artifacts into the dispatcher's world for exactly the duration of the observation -- the output was correct, faithfully transcribed, and described an environment that existed nowhere else; A CAREFUL RE-READ WOULD HAVE CONFIRMED IT, because the output was right about the constructed world. Taxonomy of measured-but-wrong: inventing a number, measuring the wrong thing, measuring the right thing in a world the test made -- all three produce sentences that read like evidence, and only the third survives re-reading. Rules: A PROBE THAT MODIFIES THE ENVIRONMENT IT MEASURES MUST SUBTRACT THE MODIFICATION before the observation ships; and the outside discriminator -- TWO OPERATORS SEEING DIFFERENT LISTS MEANS AT LEAST ONE IS AN ARTIFACT, and the surprising number gets checked first (I had the four-name reading in hand and treated the difference as machine variance instead of evidence). Bonus finding: the bin-dir-off-PATH separation was ALREADY the filter the noise report asked for -- structure doing what string matching would have approximated. | ck domain-list noise retracted; no filter built; /tmp ck-* residue flagged to BROCA. |
| THE DISCRIMINATOR STEP RUN AFTER THE RELEASE DECISION IS A FORMALITY; RUN FIRST IT IS AN INSTRUMENT (BROCA's v0.3.36): pre-measuring discriminators found ZERO strings separating new from deployed -- the release's substance was a separate operator binary the daemon never links, so the daemon "release" was a version bump dressed as a change. Rulings that followed: DO NOT PLACE a binary whose only observable is the version string (it trains the ladder to accept version-only evidence -- the habit the behavioural-witness discipline exists to break); record the version skew as fixed-on-master-not-production so the gap is not later read as a missed placement; and HAND TOOLS DO NOT ENTER THE FLEET BIN DIR -- placing an operator tool implies a currency expectation nobody will maintain, and a repair tool should always run from a fresh build of a known rev (stale placed copy strictly worse than no placed copy). The bin directory is for daemon-spawned binaries and currency-managed incident tools; a by-hand --dry-run tool is neither. | broca v0.3.36 ruled tooling-release; store-maintenance stays in the build tree; 0.3.35 stays deployed. |
| NARROWING A DESIGN TO MATCH AN IMPLEMENTATION IS AUTHORITY FLOWING BACKWARDS (bootstrap-v2 eleventh refusal, the AuthorityKeyV2 fork): the design permits three algorithms and writes explicit Ed25519 restrictions on exactly two roles; the implementation's 32-byte Ed25519-shaped field cannot represent a valid P-256/RSA status. Ruling: WIDEN THE IMPLEMENTATION -- editing the normative document to make existing code correct is the laundering direction one level up (the design gate exists so authority never flows backwards from code), and a design that demonstrably writes restrictions where it wants them makes silence on other roles DELIBERATE. Widening pins: stated restrictions become NAMED REJECTIONS (a restriction written in the design but unenforced in code is the silently-ignored-constraint class -- widening without enforcing converts deliberate restrictions into prose); negative vectors both directions (permitted role verifies, restricted role refuses by name, malformed material fails its own algorithm's arm); and the legacy narrow type does not survive as a special case (one algorithm-tagged representation, or the next author reintroduces the artifact). The it-shrinks-the-work arm distrust: twice-validated as a tell. | bootstrap-v2 key-algebra fork; slice re-cut to roster-only with three families ledgered. |
| A BACKUP IS RESIDUE ONLY AFTER THE THING IT PROTECTS IS UNWOUND-OR-ACCEPTED, AND "THE OPERATION SUCCEEDED" IS NOT ACCEPTANCE (BROCA, deleting their pre-repair store backup twenty minutes after a 1,171-row production rewrite while the downstream seat's blind measurement -- the actual acceptance gate -- was still out): a repaired row is byte-identical to one that always had the column, so THE BACKUP WAS THE ONLY ARTIFACT THAT COULD NAME WHAT THE REPAIR TOUCHED -- deleting it removed the last discriminator between repaired and never-broken, not merely a revert path. The save (data derived, recomputable from untouched WALs) was a property of the DATA, not of judgement -- right by luck, named as such. Companions: A STEP NOBODY AUTOMATED IS A STEP NOBODY CLEANED UP AFTER (twelve deliberate /tmp handoff artifacts across twelve releases -- if a handoff location is load-bearing, its hygiene needs an owner or an age sweep); and the residue worst case stated definitively: NAMES CORRECT, CONTENTS GENUINE, ONLY THE LOCATION WRONG -- no downstream instrument can tell, so location hygiene IS evidence hygiene. Correctly left standing: another seat's sample profiles named for broca's binary -- deleting another seat's evidence is the mistake the hygiene note warns against. | /tmp cleanup closed: 267 MB, 12 binaries, 4 hazard-named dirs; the deeper find was the deleted backup. |
| AD-HOC SIGNING GIVES EVERY TCC GRANT A SHELF LIFE OF ONE REBUILD (CEREB + Ufuk's live diagnosis): TCC pins grants to the binary's CDHASH because an ad-hoc signature has no stable designated requirement -- a rebuild orphans every grant SILENTLY while System Settings shows the toggle ON (the pane displays the RECORD, not whether it applies). The pinned --identifier doctrine fixed identifier churn; it cannot fix cdhash pinning -- the identifier names the row, the cdhash decides. Until a real Developer ID exists (ask_ff42466a), EVERY ck-subc PLACEMENT COSTS ONE RE-GRANT as a ladder step. Diagnosis credit: the wrong theory (stale daemon trust, needs restart) was cleanly disproven by the daemon surviving as the same pid while remove+re-add fixed it. Companions from CEREB's first live run: A DEGRADED READ SILENTLY WEAKENS EVERY CLAIM DERIVED FROM IT AND THE CLAIMS KEEP THEIR ORIGINAL WORDING (uniqueness -> uniqueness-among-what-I-read; absence unprovable from a tree that never read the subtree -- the partial-tree refusal sits BEFORE not-found); and one inaccessible element at depth 10 aborting a whole traversal read as "application closed to us" -- the depth sweep (d8-ok/d10-FAIL) was the discriminating instrument, and no fixture contains the element that only exists in real System Settings. From BROCA's stage script: A CHECK THAT ALWAYS FIRES IS THE SAME DEFECT AS ONE THAT CANNOT FIRE (1,039 string-table layout differences on a proven-unchanged release); the tool refuses to derive the marker because naming what a change introduces is a judgement; sweep by AGE not name (a version-keyed sweeper only ever knows about itself). | signing ask raised to Ufuk; accessibility partial-tree fix merged (b0143fa); stage-release.sh 3856af1. |
| DERIVE-DONT-ACCEPT MATURED FROM REMEDY INTO PREVENTION (engram's GC-fix delivery): the brief named two implementations of the protection predicate; the worker derived THREE (a worker-hydration projection the author did not know), and a fix against the author's list would have reproduced the jam in the third path -- the same incomplete-enumeration class as the harness readers and edge routes, caught this time BEFORE the gap existed. Companion: the honest-gap list has a second function -- naming the predicates deliberately NOT unified (own-entry-subtraction D semantics = a different question; legacy model; reachability-not-protection) keeps the next author from "unifying" correctly-different predicates. The complement of one-source-per-question is a recorded list of which questions are genuinely distinct. And DIGEST PARITY PROVED AS BYTES was the load-bearing gate: a protection-set digest divergence between projections presents as page-verification failures -- a worse defect than the jam, wearing the fix's name. | engram GC fix merged: 3 projections, 3 mutations killing 3 named tests, normalized closure table + backfill, EXPLAIN clean. |
| READ THE FAILURE DISTRIBUTION BEFORE THE FAILURE CAUSE (engram's post-merge near-miss): 0-passed/7-failed is a RESOURCE signature, not a logic signature -- a broken predicate reddens SPECIFIC tests; port/fixture contention uniformly wipes a suite that mostly does not touch the changed code. One flag (--test-threads=1) settled it: all 7 green serially. Pre-check on any post-merge red: uniform wipe = environment, selective redness = the change. The meta-pattern, third instance in one night: A PLAUSIBLE MECHANISM BUILT FROM ADJACENCY IS CORRECTED BY A CONTROL, NOT BY BETTER REASONING -- keep one cheap control between every adjacent-cause story and its report, and a REMEMBERED PRIOR CONTROL (this suite failed this way before, same flag settled it) is itself an instrument worth its shelf space. | engram merged-tree gate; worker extended the scoped harness rather than bypassing it. |
| WHEN AN ASK IS ABOUT ACQUIRING SOMETHING, CHECK WHETHER THE ORGANISATION ALREADY HAS IT (CEREB, after the Developer ID ask resolved in minutes): the ask was framed as a cost decision ("paid account, Ufuk's call") when it was a WHERE-IS-IT question wearing a HOW-MUCH question's clothes -- CKIOS had been publishing to TestFlight all along, so the certificate existed; the fleet is large enough that "we would need X" is frequently false. Companion binding rule (their v2 hold): A BINDING MUST ATTEST DEPLOYED REALITY -- binding signing-topology/v2 while the host's ck-subc is still ad-hoc attests a property the deployment does not have, failing later with more confidence; bind at the first placement under v2, one event, one binding, both true. And from their live a11y work: DEPTH BOUNDS TREAT THE SYMPTOM OF CYCLE-BLINDNESS -- the accessibility tree is a graph (AXApplication its own descendant, 51 deep, stack overflow KILLING the module on a caller-supplied max_depth); the fix class is identity-based cycle detection (visited set + RECORD the cut) plus iterative traversal. CORRECTED BY CEREB BEFORE THE WRONG CLAUSE SHIPPED: A CUT CYCLE IS NOT A PARTIAL READ -- re-entering an element already on the ancestor path removes a REPETITION, not content (the subgraph is already being traversed at the ancestor), so no derived claim weakens; the discriminator is IS THE UNVISITED REGION REACHABLE ELSEWHERE IN THE SAME OUTPUT (depth bound: no -> lossy, claims weaken; cycle cut: yes -> lossless, claims stand). Getting this wrong the cautious way is not safe: EVERY application carries the AXApplication self-descendant cycle, so cut-cycle-as-partial marks every tree incomplete forever, and actuation (which refuses over partial trees) could never fire -- the fixed defect re-created by the rule describing the fix. RECORD THE FACT, DO NOT WEAKEN THE CLAIM, after which depth is a cost bound rather than a survival bound -- which is what a caller-supplied parameter is allowed to be. | signing v2 rollout; a11y cycle fix with CEREB's mason. |
| THE UNIT ERROR RETURNS IN A NEW CURRENCY (engram's 4x-that-was-10%): "24-25 pages/slice all night" was a TWO-SLICE figure -- page deltas over 7-minute sampling windows spanning two ~61s slices -- compared against one-slice readings, manufacturing a 4x regression out of a ~10% cost. Same measure-in-units-of-the-event violation as the timestamp errors, now in the DENOMINATOR; caught by pulling fourteen consecutive slices instead of trusting the remembered baseline (the baseline was in the data; the 4x was in the sampling). Companions: A PATTERN THAT APPEARS IN THE WINDOW YOU ARE WATCHING IS NOT A PATTERN YOUR CHANGE INTRODUCED (pre-existing zero-page epoch-boundary slices predated the deploy; one backward scroll exonerated it) -- fourth adjacency near-miss of the night, self-caught fastest; and AN EXPLAIN PROVES WHICH INDEX IS CHOSEN, NOT THAT THE QUERY IS CHEAP -- an index makes a predicate cheap, not free, across 480k rows, and a plan-shape gate (EXPLAIN-clean) accepted as a cost gate is the two-different-claims conflation in review clothing. A 10% walk tax buying a never-worked reclamation path is a trade nobody reverses. | engram post-deploy walk cost, settled at ~10% with baselines from data; full-pass-inside-cadence is the open arithmetic. |
| A MISREAD WARNING'S REMEDY IS CALIBRATED TO THE WARNING'S WORLD, NOT YOURS (engram's gitignore near-miss): the ignore warning printed adjacent to a git add read as "the add failed", and BELIEVING it meant re-running with -f -- force-adding a path never verified untracked, a worse outcome than the imaginary problem. The add had in fact SUCCEEDED (tracked files are not subject to gitignore; git show --stat proved the commit contained the file). Warning and failure are identical from output alone; only reading the EFFECT discriminates -- and tool-printed advice (use -f; use --subc) describes the world the TOOL modeled, so following it into an unverified world converts a cosmetic misread into a real defect. Ran the effect-check specifically from having been wrong on adjacency three times in one night: corrections becoming reflexes within the session is the loop closing at its fastest. Companion from the same hour: THE SEAM RULE (FUSI's nine-tests-miss-one) -- both of the day's live-found defects were properties that exist only at a SEAM (store contents vs the number a consumer acts on; a guard correct except for a case its author never enumerated), and every test sat on one side. "Containing the right facts felt like the whole property." Ledger-worthy test question: which value does the CONSUMER act on, and does any test read THAT value from the OTHER side of the seam? | fusiform fix placed (12e4bc38, pid 73654); behavioural witness deferred by construction until the next changed poll -- prediction-match noted as not fix-proof. |
| THE FOURTH MEASURED-BUT-WRONG FORM: A REAL OBSERVATION WITH ZERO DISCRIMINATING POWER, TAKEN AS CONFIRMATION BECAUSE IT MATCHED (FUSI's interim-state read): the predicted post-placement read (version 0, counts intact) was specific, unusual, and came true -- and the OLD binary produces the identical read, so the observation was consistent with fix-present and fix-absent alike: not evidence at all. Filed as "verified my understanding of the interim state," which is true and is NOT verification of the binary. The cheap discriminating question: WHAT WOULD THE OBSERVATION HAVE LOOKED LIKE IF THE CHANGE HAD NOT BEEN MADE? If "the same", the observation is not a test -- a correct prediction is the START of an inquiry, not its end. Same idea as the constant-function mutation, wearing observation clothes (an assertion passing under both worlds distinguishes neither). Taxonomy complete: invented number / wrong thing measured / right thing in a constructed world / real thing with no discriminating power. Witness method that closed it: scratch-root drive against the PLACED binary (sha-verified first), exercising the one path production cannot reach -- testing the thing that is actually running. | fusiform witness closed same-hour; toll series 22.5s/15.4s/0.47s/0.28s trending down with host assessment history. |
| A RETRACTION'S REPLACEMENT NUMBER INHERITS CONFIDENCE IT HAS NOT EARNED (engram's 4x -> 10% -> 2x sequence): the 4x was retracted as a sampling-window error and the settled "10%, one indexed EXISTS" was published off the SAME thin base -- two post-deploy slices -- because the act of correcting feels like rigor, so the corrected figure gets less scrutiny than the original. The third consecutive slice made it a rate: 6 pages/slice against a stable 12, elapsed 60.7s -> 72.6s, per-page cost roughly DOUBLED. TWO SAMPLES LOOK LIKE BOUNDARY NOISE; THREE IS A RATE. The EXPLAIN distinction (plan gate, not cost gate) was banked and then under-weighted within the hour -- a rule's first test is usually against its own author. Trade stated concretely: full pass ~64 -> ~129 slices (~2.2h) against a WEEKLY sweep cadence = reclamation unthreatened; candidate-protected refusals: 0 = the jam is gone, the deploy's purpose served. Arm-3 optimization if the cost ever matters: protection set changes only when the generation counter moves, so a per-generation materialized set turns per-row EXISTS into one build + membership probes. | engram walk cost settled at ~2x with the per-slice instrument; not reverting; number corrected in the record over the reassuring version. |
| THE CONVERSION COST MOVED FROM THE JSON PARSE TO THE JOIN KEY (engram's 2x mechanism, named): the closure table stored object_id as TEXT because the source JSON stored hex strings -- REPRESENTATION INERTIA: migrated data keeps its source's encoding unless the migration deliberately re-keys it, and the join key is where encoding becomes cost (per-row hex(BLOB) + 32-char text probe vs 16-byte blob probe, ~480k rows = the whole 2x). The DETECTABLE form at review time: A NEW CLAUSE DIFFERING FROM ITS SIX SIBLINGS IN KEY TYPE -- six EXISTS compare BLOB=BLOB, the seventh compares TEXT=hex(BLOB); "match the siblings" was a one-line review comment nobody made because nobody compared. The six-emission-paths variant of the two-emission-paths bias. Concrete instance now attached to the plan-gate rule: EXPLAIN showed honest index use; the constant factor was invisible to it by construction. Fix: BLOB column + backfill + match siblings, success measured against the same slice_pages field, three consecutive slices minimum. | engram R43 scoped: clean, bounded, measurable -- the best kind of follow-up. |
| CORRECTNESS REVIEW AND SIBLING REVIEW ARE DIFFERENT PASSES (engram's confession on the seven EXISTS clauses): all seven were on screen during review, each read against its INTENT, none compared against EACH OTHER -- the key-type divergence (six BLOB=BLOB, one TEXT=hex) was visible the whole time and invisible to the pass being run. The sibling-comparison pass must be run DELIBERATELY; having the siblings in view does not perform it. Same shape as reading a log line for its family instead of its sequence. Paired with the detector it completes: a new clause differing from its siblings in key type/shape is a one-line review comment IF the comparing pass runs. | engram review retro; R43 running; fusiform's first portable-class capture (7-not-6 entries) is tonight's live test of the stated dependency. |
| BEFORE ATTRIBUTING A MECHANISM TO AN ABSENCE, DATE THE THING WHOSE ABSENCE YOU ARE EXPLAINING (engram's fusiform-discovery retraction, fourth adjacency error of the night): five generations at entry_count=6 read as "discovery failed structurally" when the descriptor's mtime postdated every generation examined -- one ls would have said so; the exonerating timestamp existed in the filesystem the whole time. My relay was wrong the same way with a different file: I dated the DATA HOME's creation and reasoned about boot-cache discovery, when the discriminating artifact was the DESCRIPTOR's mtime inside it -- right method, wrong file. Standing gap, correctly separated from the retraction: a descriptor written but not yet carried has NO POSITIVE SIGNAL (unprotectedModules reads discovery's own output -- the self-referential gate again); the independent-enumeration diff (data-root filesystem listing vs published manifest entries) is one witness closing BOTH failure shapes: the structural miss tonight was not, and the enrolled-but-not-yet-carried window it actually was. | fusiform enrollment: timing miss, not discovery defect; 7-entry witness pending on the next capture; 0600 descriptor note to FUSI. |
| RENAME-AFTER-VERIFY MAKES ROW-DROP UNREACHABLE RATHER THAN UNLIKELY (engram's R43 closure migration): validate every source row with four INDEPENDENT malformedness checks (type, length, charset GLOB, unhex-null), insert into a NEW table, prove membership with a NOT EXISTS anti-join, and only then rename old aside / new into place -- the old data survives until verification passes, so a conversion that silently dropped rows (which would un-protect objects and reproduce the exact jam the prior fix closed -- the failure mode wearing the fix's name) is structurally impossible instead of tested-against. Companions: parity across THREE projections with digests compared AS BYTES (a storage change must not move the digest; proving it did not is what makes it a storage change); explicit runtime-function availability check (workerd unhex) -- assuming the full SQLite function set at the edge is the class that fails only in production; and the worker's own report declining to claim the throughput restoration only production can measure. | R43 merged; hypothesis rests on three consecutive post-deploy slice_pages readings per the pre-registered floor. |

| A GATE WRITTEN FOR ONE DIRECTION CONSTRAINS A CAPABILITY THAT DOES NOT EXIST YET, AND IS BETTER EVIDENCE THAN A DESIGN NOTE (CEREB's launch-path find): the custody gate forbids --remote-debugging-port/-address, written for the ATTACH path before any launcher existed -- so the future launcher is FORCED onto --remote-debugging-pipe by a refusal list that says "pipe, not port" to code not yet written, with teeth. Security framing to preserve verbatim: A TCP DEBUGGING PORT IS AN UNAUTHENTICATED CONTROL CHANNEL (CDP has no auth step; loopback narrows reachability to "every process on this machine", no reduction worth the name for a browser holding live logins; a pipe's two inherited descriptors make reachability a property of PROCESS ANCESTRY rather than network position). Fleet check worth running: existing refusal lists are design constraints with teeth -- read them before writing the capability they will govern. Launch-surface positions ruled as fleet doctrine: orphans REFUSED not adopted (unattested process state; boot-boundary applied to children); contention = TYPED refusal never serialization (an invisible queue is the deferral-starvation class); launch is its OWN capability never implicit-on-first-use (explicit-lease doctrine one rung up); executables PINNED in config never PATH-discovered (the /tmp incident's lesson), absent/mismatch refused naming expected AND found incl. signature identity. | cerebellum launch-path spec firing; SUBC review covers it, custody-gate widenings escalate to Ufuk. |
| A MISSING VERDICT IS NOT A PASS (engram's wasm gate): the CI batch hit its 30-minute cap MID-GATE, so the output ended after the step header with no verdict -- and truncated-at-the-header reads exactly like all-green to anyone scanning for red. The interrupted gate re-run ALONE is the only honest completion; the terminal-event rule (a stall and a finish look identical without the terminal line) applied to gate output. Companion, the discard-rule discipline: when a known one-time cost (first-wake migration) will land inside the measurement window, STATE THE DISCARD BEFORE SEEING THE NUMBER -- a pre-registered discard is methodology, a post-hoc one is an excuse, and the difference is only the timestamp on the statement. | engram R43 deployed (4afc9db5); hypothesis measurement running against the pre-registered 6/slice baseline. |
| WHEN ONE ARM OF A DESIGN FORK IS ALSO THE ARM THAT AVOIDS BUILDING SOMETHING, THE COINCIDENCE IS EVIDENCE ABOUT THE REASONING, NOT THE DESIGN (CEREB's generalization of the work-shrinking tell): it does not make the arm wrong -- it means the argument for it must survive being made by someone with nothing to gain. Companion practice from the same exchange: FOLD REASONS, NOT VERDICTS into a spec -- a panel that sees only "adopt: no" re-derives the argument and sometimes reaches the other answer; the reason travels, the verdict does not. Launch-lifetime rulings for the record: lease-bound life (explicit close capability, idle deadline visible at grant time, unbind as the reaping backstop -- a launched child never outlives its supervisor); disposable-profile crash debris swept at startup keyed on the module's OWN mint-manifest, never directory-shape heuristics (reclaim what you can prove you created); STALE LOCKS breakable on pid+kernel-start-time evidence recorded INTO the lock at acquisition, break logged WITH the evidence, break-then-acquire atomic (loser gets profile_busy naming the WINNER) -- so profile_busy always names a live holder or the lock is breakable, closing unreachable-forever from both sides. | cerebellum launch spec ct_...02ad56e0f6d0 round 1; two late questions pre-resolved. |
| THE HOLE IS BETWEEN THE RULINGS, NOT IN EITHER OF THEM (CEREB's stale-lock composition find): terminate-not-adopt and typed-refusal-naming-the-holder are each correct, and together they LOCK AN AGENT OUT OF ITS OWN DURABLE PROFILE PERMANENTLY after one unclean shutdown -- nothing to terminate, a named holder that does not exist, every individual refusal right. The paired-suppression class (two correct branches, nobody owns the pair) elevated to design rulings -- and it surfaced ONLY when the rulings were written into one document, which makes folding-reasons-into-one-draft a HAZARD DETECTOR rather than mere hygiene. Companions: TOCTOU-ON-A-PROOF (two sessions truthfully prove the same lock stale; the evidence stays valid while the ACTION races -- no better evidence closes it, only atomicity); and the attestation boundary for third-party locks: our staleness mechanism attests only locks WE minted -- a foreign lock is unattestable by construction, so a live foreign holder gets its own refusal (held-externally, not busy) and is never broken (breaking an unattestable lock is adoption wearing a cleanup costume), while any staleness proof built over a third-party lock format inherits format drift (the vendored-fixture class pointed at a lock file). | cerebellum launch spec re-fired (ct_...02926089c4c8), 13 pre-resolved, 17 acceptance items, one question left for the panel with its constraint stated. |

Repaired rule: WHEN INPUTS ARRIVE BECAUSE YOU SOLICIT THEM, THE STOPPING CONDITION MUST BE A COMMITMENT, NOT A QUIET SIGNAL -- late arrivals merge at harvest, where merging is already routine. Companion vocabulary rule: TWO REFUSALS THAT A FUTURE READER WILL MERGE NEED THEIR DISTINCTION STATED AS REMEDIES-AND-AUDIENCES (profile_busy = wait-or-choose, module can name the holder; profile_held_externally = a human is using that browser, only they decide) with both-directions acceptance so one implementation returning one name for both fails. | A DEFERRAL INHERITS THE SCOPE OF THE QUESTION THAT PRODUCED IT (cke2e's status-family unblock, the phantom-marker shape's second instance): the worker correctly reported that the BRIEF'S stated input could not confer semantics, and the author generalized it to "status has no producer" -- a claim about the world made from a claim about a brief. Companion decomposition move for set-membership questions: CHECK WHICH DIRECTION IS ALREADY CLOSED BY CONSTRUCTION -- a carried element failing resolution is already a rejection (MissingWitness), so subset-vs-equality reduces to the single open direction (may the epoch OMIT a ledger-held record), and a cap prerequisite named "complete-...-history" is the evidence lean on that direction -- read what the prerequisite OBLIGATES before declaring the design silent. | bootstrap-v2 status family unblocked via trace; subset question routed to the prerequisite's definition. |
| A NAMED PROPERTY'S DEFINITION IS FOUND BY SEARCHING THE PROPERTY'S PHRASE, NOT BY READING THE ARTIFACT THAT CITES IT (cke2e's equality settlement): the cap prerequisite string named "complete-enrollment-status-history" without defining it; the definition lived in section prose seventeen lines from where they were reading -- the ONLY hit for the phrase in the document. The citation carries the name; the prose carries the meaning. The proof itself is a keeper: BOUNDS-IDENTITY COLLAPSES SUBSET TO EQUALITY (a 6..12 selection from a 6..12 history that may not omit IS the history -- if subset were legal the epoch's bound would be narrower or unbounded below), reinforced by the design naming the escape and killing it in one breath ("there is no checkpoint alternative" -- a subset is a checkpoint by another name). | A REAL DEFECT CAN BE A DECOY FOR THE DOMINANT COST (engram's refuted BLOB hypothesis, reported on the pre-registered arm): the type mismatch was genuine -- six siblings BLOB=BLOB, one TEXT=hex(BLOB), found by the sibling detector -- and fixing it recovered NOTHING (5-6 pages/slice against a 6 baseline; the pre-registered refutation arm fired and was reported as the result). The magnitude was ASSUMED FROM VISIBILITY: a per-row hex() reads expensive, but the dominant cost was the SEVENTH CORRELATED SUBQUERY ITSELF -- adding an EXISTS to a per-row CASE across 480k objects costs roughly what it costs regardless of key encoding. Distinct from the ordinary decoy: this one was a true defect sitting ON the mechanism, and fixing it was still right (siblings match, migration verified, reverting to restore a cost is not an improvement) -- the fix doubling as the refutation experiment was the cheapest way to learn the truth. Visibility is not magnitude; a found defect's PRICE needs its own measurement before it wears the anomaly's name. | engram walk cost: BLOB stays, materialized-protected-set parked as optimization on a working path; jam remains gone (zero refusals). |
| A WITNESS THAT REQUIRES A MONTH OF PATIENCE IS NOT A WITNESS, IT IS A HOPE (engram, on the first-D-pass timeline): the arc's "witness" was ~27 days out by cadence -- believing verification was SCHEDULED when it was merely POSSIBLE is the trap. Witnesses decompose into three states: PROVEN (jam gone, zero refusals), REACHABLE (the Q-plan discriminator -- one deliberate gc.run away; schedule it, do not wait for cadence), and GRACE-BOUND BY DESIGN (the D pass cannot fire before the 21-day retention grace elapses, and any path reaching it sooner means weakening a safety fence to satisfy a verification appetite -- testing-in-prod wearing rigor's clothes). The graduation rule: after the reachable witness fires, the grace-bound one stops being hope and becomes a DATED expectation -- the difference between waiting and scheduling. Deploy fatigue is a reason to not act TODAY, never a reason to leave the act unscheduled: name the day and the option stops being a thing discovered later. | engram GC: jam proven, Q-plan scheduled-not-awaited, D-pass dated after Q fires. |

| A SHIPPED, GREEN, STRUCTURALLY IDENTICAL SIBLING IS THE CHEAPEST ORACLE AVAILABLE (cke2e's status unblock, third resolution in one investigation): the 29-equal/11-differ field measurement put RosterRecord in the same recipe-wrapper class as the "blocked" status family -- and roster SHIPPED with exactly that structure, refuting "the structure blocks status" in bytes rather than prose. When a family looks unbuildable, check whether a sibling with the same wire shape already ships BEFORE another prose pass. | AN ACCOUNT-WIDE ANSWER TO A PER-DEVICE OBLIGATION (engram R44, the data-loss class R42 could not reach): the migration gate keyed on registryEntries != 0 -- an ACCOUNT count -- so the first device to register silenced every sibling's walker ("not_pending"), their historical closures never entered the ProtectiveIndex, and D-phase reads a chunk shared with an unregistered sibling's retained generation as EXCLUSIVE: deletion while retention still promises restore, ordinary serial upgrade as trigger, no race required. The camouflage: a CORRECT-LOOKING early return -- "the registry already has entries, nothing to migrate" is a reasonable sentence whose subject is the WRONG SCOPE. The shared-helper class inverted into state: one gate, N obligated parties, the first satisfier silencing the rest. Scope-of-the-question audit: for every early return, ask WHOSE obligation the gate discharges and whether its predicate reads at the same scope. Meta-note: R44 found this because the round was SCOPED TO THE CLASS ("something deleted while retention needs it") -- availability-scoped R42 structurally could not.
